title: Helical Keratin‐Derived Aqueous Binders for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
content:
This study introduces a green, aqueous binder combining helical proteins, polyvinyl alcohol, and glycerol for lithium‐sulfur batteries. The protein's “molecular spring” structure effectively buffers volume expansion, while its polar groups strongly anchor polysulfides to suppress the shuttle effect and boost redox kinetics. This synergistic design ultimately enables exceptional long‐term cycling stability.








ABSTRACT
Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) possess ultrahigh energy density, low cost, and environmental friendliness, making them strong contenders for next‐generation energy storage technologies. However, their development is hindered by multiple interfacial challenges, including the shuttling of lithium polysulfides (LiPS), sluggish reaction kinetics, and severe volume expansion of the cathode. To address these issues, a multifunctional biomass‐derived aqueous binder was designed by crosslinking an α‐helical protein (α‐HP) with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and glycerol (GL). The α ‐helical structure of α‐HP in the α‐HP/PVA/GL adhesive acts as a “molecular spring”, effectively buffering volume expansion and stabilizing the electrode structure. Additionally, its abundant N‐ and O‐containing polar groups efficiently anchor LiPS, significantly suppressing the shuttling effect and accelerating redox kinetics. Consequently, lithium‐sulfur batteries employing the α‐HP/PVA/GL binder exhibit exceptional long‐term cycling stability. The α‐HP/PVA/GL cathode delivers an initial discharge specific capacity of 737.3 mAh g−1 and retains 487.9 mAh g−1 after 600 stable cycles at 2 C, with an average capacity decay rate of only 0.056% per cycle. This study provides a green, facile, and efficient strategy for developing multifunctional binders to overcome practical bottlenecks in lithium‐sulfur battery applications.

title: Mechanochemically Disordered Li2Ta2OCl10 Oxyhalide Unlocks Superionic Conductivity (>10 mS.cm−1)
content:
This work presents a new crystalline oxyhalide, Li2Ta2OCl10, built from [Ta2OCl10]2− dimers. The disorder induced by ball‐milling drives the dramatic 5000‐fold increase in ionic conductivity to reach 11 mS.cm−1. The material shows promise as a solid electrolyte for batteries and opens new prospects for the discovery of new dimer‐based compounds.








ABSTRACT
All‐solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries (ASSBs) offer a promising route to surpass the energy‐density limits of conventional lithium‐ion technology. However, their commercialization is hindered by interfacial instability, chemo‐mechanical degradation, and the limited ionic conductivity of current solid electrolytes, driving the search for new fast‐ion conductors, particularly among lithium oxyhalides. Here, we report a new lithium tantalum oxychloride, Li2Ta2OCl10, synthesized via a simple low‐temperature route. The material crystallizes in a triclinic structure composed of isolated [Ta2OCl10]2− dimers and exhibits a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 0.002 mS.cm−1. Ball milling dramatically enhances Li+ transport, increasing the conductivity by a factor of 5000 to 11 mS.cm−1 while reducing the activation energy from 0.46 to 0.27 eV. Combined structural, spectroscopic, and computational analyses reveal that this enhancement originates from the formation of a highly disordered, liquid‐like Li+ sublattice. Li2Ta2OCl10 further demonstrates a stability window of 1.89–3.70 V vs. LixIn and enables ASSBs with low polarization and excellent capacity retention (700 cycles at 1C with decay less than 20%). These results establish Li2Ta2OCl10 as a promising superionic conductor and highlight the Li–M–O–Cl family as a fertile design space for next‐generation solid electrolytes.

title: Trash to Treasure: PFAS‐Functionalized MOFs for Boosted Piezocatalytic H2 Production
content:
A novel pollutant‐as‐functional‐additive strategy is developed via postsynthetic modification of MOF‐808(Hf) with perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA), a typical PFAS pollutant. The modification boosts the dipole moment of the MOFs, enhances their piezoelectricity to promote efficient electron‐hole separation, thus delivering ultrahigh piezocatalytic hydrogen evolution activity, with broad universality for Hf‐based MOFs bearing unsaturated metal sites.








ABSTRACT
Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) hold broad prospects in piezocatalysis because of their high surface area, porosity, and tunable structures, yet pristine MOFs frequently suffer from poor piezocatalytic response. Herein, this study pioneers a novel strategy using pollutant perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) as a functional additive to post‐synthetically modify MOF‐808(Hf), fabricating MOF‐808(Hf)‐F for piezocatalytic hydrogen production. PFHxA modification remarkably enhances the polarity of MOF‐808(Hf) (dipole moment from 8.90 to 12.58 D) and piezoelectricity (d33 from 63.70 to 234.30 pm V−1), boosting electron‐hole separation verified by electrochemical and in situ photoluminescence characterizations. Consequently, MOF‐808(Hf)‐F achieves an excellent piezocatalytic H2 evolution rate of 2811.4 µmol g−1 h−1, 10.5‐fold higher than the pristine counterpart and superior to that of numerous reported MOF‐based piezocatalysts. In addition, MOF‐808(Hf) achieves a PFHxA removal efficiency of approximately 40.1% from water. This work realizes simultaneous per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) removal and efficient energy production, with excellent universality for Hf‐based MOFs with unsaturated metal sites.

title: 16.52% Efficiency All‐Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells via Al‐Doped ZnO/SnO2 Electron Transport Bilayer for Improved Interfacial Energy‐Level Alignment
content:
This work reports a new approach in enhancing efficiency of CsPbI2Br perovskite solar cells by introducing Al‐doped ZnO/SnO2 electron transport bilayer for improved interfacial energy‐level alignment without doping or passivation of the perovskite, without resorting passivation or doping the perovskites, leading to a champion power conversion efficiency of 16.52% along with a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.33 V.








ABSTRACT
Interfacial energy‐level misalignment in all‐inorganic perovskite solar cells generally causes inefficient charge extraction. Here, we propose an Al‐doped ZnO (AZO)/SnO2 electron transport bilayer to improve energy‐level alignment in CsPbI2Br‐based PSCs. By this approach, we achieved a champion efficiency of 16.52%, which is the highest reported value for all‐inorganic CsPbI2Br PSCs without doping or passivation of the perovskite, along with a high VOC of 1.33 V. AZO‐based devices substantially outperform ZnO‐based controls, delivering a PCE of 16.52% versus 15.21%, with suppressed dark current, reduced trap density, lower non‐radiative recombination, and smaller hysteresis. The AZO device retains 80% of its initial efficiency after 662 h of continuous illumination, compared with only 312 h for the ZnO counterpart. Al3+ substitution for Zn2+ elevates the ZnO conduction band minimum, establishing a favorable cascade alignment among SnO2/AZO/perovskite that lowers the electron extraction barrier and blocks hole backflow. Al doping also suppresses oxygen vacancies, reducing interfacial trap‐state density and enhancing perovskite crystallinity. Efficient charge extraction further suppresses Ag electrode degradation and corrosion, contributing to long‐term stability. This work establishes a rational interfacial engineering approach using an AZO/SnO2 bilayer for efficient and stable all‐inorganic perovskite solar cells.

title: Scanless Centimeter‐Scale Microstereolithography Enabled by Source‐Plane Angular Conditioning
content:
A source‐plane angular‐conditioning (SPAC) architecture enables efficient coupling of a large‐area LCD to finite‐aperture projection optics, overcoming the conventional resolution–area trade‐off in projection microstereolithography. The proposed LµSL platform achieves micron‐scale projected pixels and centimeter‐scale fabrication in a single exposure without stitching or mechanical scanning.








ABSTRACT
Achieving centimeter‐scale scanless microstereolithography remains challenging in conventional projection microstereolithography (PµSL), where improving resolution inevitably restricts printable area due to the finite number of pixels. High‐pixel‐density LCD modulators provide a promising pathway to relax this limitation, but their large emission area introduces severe optical coupling and illumination nonuniformity in reduction projection systems. Here, we introduce source‐plane angular conditioning implemented in an LCD‐based microstereolithography (LµSL) platform. This optical strategy reshapes the emission angular distribution of a planar light source, enabling efficient pupil matching and uniform wide‐field illumination for scanless projection across centimeter‐scale areas. Using an 8K LCD modulator and wide‐angle lenses with different focal lengths, the system achieves projected pixel pitches of ≈1–3 µm over printable areas of ≈0.8–2.4 cm in a single exposure without mechanical scanning, stitching, or relay optics. Diverse microstructures—including stripe arrays, microneedle arrays, octet‐truss lattices, and complex freeform geometries—are fabricated to demonstrate the platform's capability for heterogeneous, multi‐scale microfabrication. The proposed optical framework establishes a practical route toward high‐resolution, large‐area microfabrication and provides a scalable platform for applications in microfluidics, biomedical devices, photonics, and architected materials.

title: Polarity‐Mediated β‐Phase Reconstruction and Dual‐Salt Synergy for Fast Li+ Transport in Solid‐State Li Metal Batteries
content:
Molecular‐polarity synergy combining TCNE‐driven β‐phase reconstruction and dualsalt engineering optimizes ion transport and interphase, enabling high‐performance PVDF solid polymer electrolytes for long‐life lithium‐metal batteries.








ABSTRACT
Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) based on poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) hold great promise for safe Li metal batteries but are hindered by low ionic conductivity and insufficient salt dissociation. Here, we propose a molecular polarity‐mediated synergistic strategy that integrates tetracyanoethylene (TCNE)‐induced β‐phase reconstruction with dual‐salt chemistry to simultaneously optimize ion transport kinetics and interfacial stability. In this strategy, the strongly electron‐withdrawing cyano groups of TCNE engage in dipole interactions with PVDF chains, triggering a nonpolar α‐to‐polar β‐phase transition, which facilitates salt dissociation and shortens the Li+ migration pathway; the dual‐salt system further ensures fast Li+ conduction while constructing a robust, LiF/boron‐rich interphase via LiDFOB. The resulting TCNE‐modified PVDF electrolyte (PTDL) delivers a high ionic conductivity of 9.32 × 10−4 S cm−1, a high Li+ transference number of 0.76, and a wide electrochemical window of 4.8 V. Thus, the symmetric cells can maintain a low overpotential over 1000 h at 0.2 mA cm−2, and full cells with LiFePO4 cathode can run stably for 1000 cycles at 10 C. This work provides a new path for designing high‐performance PVDF‐based SPEs.

title: Multilayer 3D/2D Perovskite Heterojunctions: Structural Engineering, Interfacial Modulation, and Photovoltaic Applications
content:
This review examines how interface location, phase composition, and crystal orientation govern the performance of multilayer 3D/2D perovskite heterojunctions. It connects structural design with defect passivation, selective charge transport, and suppressed ion migration, highlighting strategies for improving solar cell efficiency and stability and advancing applications in large‐area modules, tandem solar cells, and flexible devices.








ABSTRACT
Perovskite solar cells combine excellent optoelectronic properties with solution processability, but their long‐term performance remains limited by interfacial defects, ion migration and structural instability. Multilayer 3D/2D perovskite heterojunctions offer a promising route to address these limitations by integrating efficient light absorption and charge transport of three‐dimensional perovskites with defect passivation effect and high stability of two‐dimensional perovskites. However, poorly controlled formation of low‐dimensional phases usually introduce mixed dimensionalities, unfavorable orientations, excessive organic spacers and energetic barriers, thereby compromising charge extraction and long‐term stability. Here, we review the evolution of multilayer 3D/2D heterojunctions in terms of interface location, phase composition and crystallographic orientation, and compare solution, thermal evaporation, imprint‐transfer and vapor‐assisted fabrication strategies. We further discuss their roles in defect passivation, energy‐level regulation, charge transport, phase‐structure control and phase stabilization, and highlight their emerging applications in large‐area modules, tandem and flexible devices. Finally, we outline key opportunities in deterministic phase control, interface‐specific asymmetric design, operando characterization, and scalable fabrication to advance multilayer 3D/2D heterojunctions from empirical interface modification toward rationally engineered and manufacturable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Depth‐Aware Machine Learning for 3D Reconstruction of Fibrous Porous Electrodes by FIB‐SEM Tomography
content:
In FIB–SEM tomography of highly porous polymeric electrodes, subsurface fibers visible through open pores are mistaken for in‐plane material, distorting 3D reconstructions. A machine‐learning‐based depth‐aware model trained on everyday photographs, combined with unsupervised clustering, isolates the exposed fiber cross‐sections without labeled data, agreeing more closely with experimental benchmarks.








ABSTRACT
Quantitative three‐dimensional reconstruction of porous polymers with sub‐micrometer feature sizes is central to understanding and designing electrochemical interfaces and membranes. However, focused ion beam–scanning electron microscopy tomography combined with conventional segmentation techniques cannot readily reconstruct complex disordered morphologies such as fibers. Standard segmentation workflows misclassify out‐of‐plane material as in‐plane material, distorting the reconstructed pore network, fiber connectivity, and interface area. Here, we introduce an annotation‐free, depth‐aware machine‐learning framework that combines monocular depth estimation, trained on macroscale images, with unsupervised clustering to separate in‐plane polymer cross‐sections from subsurface contributions in serial FIB–SEM tomography images. Applied to copper‐coated electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) fiber mats, the approach produces 3D reconstructions that preserve fibrous morphology more faithfully than conventional supervised and unsupervised segmentation. Quantitative validation against capillary flow porometry, pycnometry, and high‐resolution wide‐angle X‐ray computed tomography demonstrates improved agreement across pore cross‐section diameter, fiber volume ratio, and Cu depth decrease metrics. This work establishes depth‐aware segmentation as a transferable strategy from real‐scale to nanoscale imaging, requiring no labeled training data and enabling accurate 3D segmentation and reconstruction from SEM images. This approach opens a path toward more reliable structure–property relationships in disordered porous polymer materials.

title: Adaptive Ferroic Bi‐Sb Hybrid Iodides for Multi‐Modal Energy Harvesting and Phototronics
content:
Composition‐driven lattice engineering in 1D hybrid iodides, HDABiI5 (HBI), HDASbI5 (HSI), and HDABi0.5Sb0.5I5 (HBSI), allows control over symmetry, lattice dynamics, ferroic order, charge transport, and thermal stability. Bi/Sb substitution modulates polarization, electronic structure, and coupled functional responses. A HBI‐HSI‐HBSI trilayer synergistically integrates piezo‐, tribo‐, pyro‐, thermo‐, ferro‐, and photonic effects, delivering 5.1‐fold enhanced current generation.








ABSTRACT
Organic–inorganic hybrid halides offer a versatile platform for programmable multimodal functionalities, through structural softness and lattice‐charge coupling, despite the challenge of balancing the competing ferroic order, carrier transport, and thermal stability requirements. We present a composition‐driven lattice engineering strategy in a 1D iodide series based on 1,6‐diaminohexane (HDA), comprising orthorhombic non‐centrosymmetric phases of HDABiI5 (HBI) and HDASbI5 (HSI) together with a lower‐symmetry non‐centrosymmetric monoclinic phase of HDABi0.5Sb0.5I5 (HBSI) identified by its birefringent response, allowing systematic control of symmetry, lattice dynamics, and coupled transport phenomena. Through variable‐temperature crystallography and 1H NMR, multi‐perturbation Raman spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, photophysical measurements, and electronic structure calculations, we demonstrate a progression from a rigid Bi‐dominated lattice exhibiting strong piezoelectric and ferroelectric coupling to a softer Sb‐rich framework with enhanced anharmonicity, pyroelectricity, and photonic activity, while HBSI combines efficient thermal robustness and phonon transport. Density functional theory calculations show that Bi/Sb substitution tunes the electronic structure from indirect to direct bandgap, modulates oscillator strength, spontaneous polarization, pressure‐dependent electronic properties, thermoelectric and piezoelectric responses, while preserving low iodine‐vacancy formation energies. A trilayer HBI‐HSI‐HBSI architecture couples piezoelectric, triboelectric, pyroelectric, thermoelectric, ferroelectric, and photonic effects, showing 5.1‐fold synergistic enhancement in current generation through interfacial polarization and multimodal coupling.

title: Resolving the Structural Origin of Lattice Oxygen Release across Scales in Practical Lithium‐Manganese‐Rich Electrodes
content:
Gas measurements capture only the collective outcome of reactions across an electrode, leaving the structural origin of oxygen release hidden. This work maps manganese reduction, a fingerprint of oxygen release, from electrode to grain by combining online mass spectrometry with multi‐scale X‐ray and electron microscopy. Grain‐facet exposure, not electrode or particle structure, emerges as its key structural descriptor.








ABSTRACT
Gas evolution from lattice oxygen release is a major obstacle to deployment of high‐energy‐density cathodes, yet its structural origin within dense electrodes remains challenging to resolve across multiple length scales. This difficulty arises because gas evolution is the collective outcome of oxygen release from numerous grains and particles, whose environments can vary across electrode, secondary‐particle, and grain scales. Here, by integrating online electrochemical mass spectrometry with synchrotron X‐ray and electron microscopy, this study resolves the spatial origin of O2 evolution through mapping Mn reduction, a chemical fingerprint of oxygen release, across four orders of magnitude in length scale. Two lithium‐manganese‐rich layered oxide (LMR) electrodes that vary only in secondary‐particle size are employed as a model system, and their O2 evolution differs twofold. Spatially resolving Mn oxidation state distribution reveals no detectable Mn‐reduction gradient across the electrode thickness or within particles, indicating that the difference does not originate from electrode‐ or particle‐scale heterogeneity. Instead, frontal facets (lithium‐intercalation planes) of grains exhibit deeper Mn reduction and surface reconstruction than lateral facets, consistent with favorable oxygen vacancy formation and migration. O2 evolution matches after frontal‐facet area normalization, identifying frontal‐facet exposure as a key structural descriptor for O2 evolution in these practical LMR electrodes.

title: Regioisomerism‐Guided Molecular Passivation for 26.05%‐Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
Among three fluoroaniline regioisomers, 2‐fluoroaniline (2‐FA), featuring an intramolecular NH···F hydrogen bond, exhibits the most robust surface affinity and defect passivation, yielding a power conversion efficiency exceeding 26%. This regioisomerism‐guided strategy is universally applicable to both n‐i‐p and p‐i‐n architectures, regardless of one‐step or two‐step perovskite fabrication.








ABSTRACT
Defect‐mediated nonradiative recombination remains a major barrier to efficient and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Although considerable advances have been made with molecular additives, how the spatial arrangement of functional groups affects device performance remains largely unexplored. Here, we present a regioisomerism‐guided molecular design strategy using fluorinated aniline as a well‐defined model system to incorporate into the lead iodide (PbI2) precursor solution during two‐step sequential perovskite deposition. By systematically comparing ortho‐, meta‐, and para‐fluoroaniline, we demonstrate that the ortho isomer, 2‐fluoroaniline (2‐FA), affords the most effective regulation of defect states and device performance. This superiority arises from the formation of an intramolecular hydrogen bond, which redistributes the molecular electrostatic potential and confers stable bidentate coordination with the perovskite lattice. Additionally, 2‐FA facilitates high‐quality α‐FAPbI3 films and aligns the energy level favorably with the hole transport layer, yielding a champion efficiency of 26.05% for the n‐i‐p PSCs. Moreover, the 2‐FA‐containing device exhibits superior operational stability. This regioisomerism‐guided design works universally across n‐i‐p and p‐i‐n architectures, irrespective of one‐step or two‐step fabrication. Our work establishes regioisomerism as a simple yet powerful molecular design principle for molecular engineering and provides new insight into the rational development of efficient and stable PSCs.

title:
Regioselective Growth
of Mesoporous Metal–Organic
Frameworks for the Construction of Anisotropic Nanohybrids
content:
Abstract
Mesoporous anisotropic nanohybrids (m-ANHs) have attracted growing interest because their structural asymmetry enables unique advantages in applications such as multidrug co-delivery and cascade catalysis. However, anisotropic growth in mesoporous systems has thus far been largely confined to an amorphous framework. Achieving regioselective growth of crystalline functional units integrated with mesoporous frameworks remains highly challenging, primarily because of the intrinsic competition at the heterointerface between crystal nucleation/deposition and micelle-directed mesostructural coassembly. Herein, we report an acidity-gated interfacial crystallization-coassembly switching strategy to construct single-crystalline mesoporous MOF (meso-MOF)-based ANHs. This strategy enables the site-selective growth of a new single-crystalline meso-MOF compartment at predefined heterointerfaces, yielding a diverse family of well-defined frame-like, dumbbell-like, and ternary spiny nanohybrids. Mechanistically, precise regulation of the HCl/CH3COOH ratio modulates the nucleation kinetics of MOF precursors, generating localized supersaturation that is sufficient to trigger site-selective heterogeneous nucleation. Concurrently, synchronization of MOF nucleation/growth with interfacial micelle-directed coassembly allows crystallization and mesopore organization to proceed cooperatively. The applicability of this interfacial regulation is demonstrated in several lattice-compatible and chemically stable MOF systems with different compositions and hybrid configurations. As a proof of concept, the hierarchical spiny topology significantly enhances physical bacteria–material interactions, endowing the ternary ANHs with superior antibacterial performance. Remarkably, even in the absence of any drug loading, the ANHs achieve an approximately 90% inhibition efficiency against drug-resistant bacteria. This work establishes a versatile route to regioselectively integrate single-crystalline mesoporous domains into complex anisotropic nanohybrids and highlights the functional potential of structurally programmed crystalline mesoporous interfaces.

title:
Assisted Tandem Catalysis
with M–M Bonded Heterobimetallic
Pd–Pt Complexes: Accessing Both Pd and Pt Catalytic Cycles
content:
Abstract
We report the synthesis of M–M bonded Pd–Pt complexes at the Pd(I)/Pt(I) and Pd(I)/Pt(III) oxidation states. These bimetallic complexes act as a reservoir for catalytically active Pd and Pt centers, and catalysis is observed in a variety of Pd- and Pt-catalyzed reactions. We demonstrate that tandem catalytic reactions with our Pd(I)/Pt(I) complex can capitalize on both Pd and Pt catalytic cycles to enable multistep processes. These include tandem hydrosilylation/Hiyama coupling, Suzuki coupling/amide reduction, Buchwald–Hartwig amination/amide reduction, and Heck coupling/amide reduction. Tandem cycloisomerization/Heck coupling is also observed with our Pd(I)/Pt(III) complex. Control studies demonstrate that homobimetallic Pd–Pd and Pt–Pt complexes do not perform the tandem catalytic reactions and that the Pd–Pt complex is stable under air and moisture for at least 9 months. The M–M bond in these complexes enables access to unique Pd and Pt oxidation states and facilitates M–M communication, both of which can have an impact during catalysis.

title:
Pressure-Induced Single-Crystal-to-Single-Crystal
Dimerization and Irreversible Optical Reconstruction in a 2D Hybrid
Lead Halide
content:
Abstract
External pressure is a powerful tool for tuning hybrid metal halides (HMHs), yet the resulting structural and optical changes are usually reversible upon decompression. Locking pressure-accessed states through covalent bond formation, particularly while preserving single-crystallinity and optical functionality, remains challenging. Here, we report a pressure-induced single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SC-SC) [2 + 2] dimerization in a two-dimensional lead halide, (S-MAMBA)2PbBr4, which contains acrylate-functionalized S-MAMBA+ cations. This process yields a stable dimerized single-crystal phase upon decompression. The topochemically preorganized arrangement of S-MAMBA+ enables irreversible cyclobutane formation while preserving the crystallinity. High-pressure vibrational and diffraction measurements, together with recovered single-crystal structure determination, establish the pressure-induced bond-forming transformation. During compression, the emission evolves from self-trapped exciton (STE)-dominated to free-exciton (FE)-dominated recombination near the dimerization threshold, indicating a reconstructed excitonic pathway. After decompression, the dimerized phase shows irreversible optical reconstruction, characterized by opposite absorption and emission shifts. Density functional theory (DFT) reveals that this chemical transformation perturbs the inorganic-framework band-edge electronic structure through changes in organic–inorganic interactions and interlayer coupling. This work demonstrates that pressure can be used as a novel and powerful trigger for permanent bond and electronic structure reconstruction in hybrid materials.

title:
Quantum Ghost Spectroscopy
Reveals Hidden Coherence
in Molecular Aggregates
content:
Abstract
Ultrafast spectroscopy of complex molecules has been achieved under light–matter coupling by the use of laser pulses and single photons. Yet, the excited-state dynamics essential to photochemistry is suffering from the convolution of multiple relaxation pathways and limited resolution in nonlinear signal, which still remain challenging. To address these, we develop time-resolved quantum ghost spectroscopy (tr-QGS) with entangled light, which enables a background-free detection of excited-state emission while offering precise control over temporal resolution. We apply this approach to perylene bisimide (PBI-1) trimers by combining a quantum description of light-molecule interaction with time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (TD-DMRG) simulations. This explicitly includes five vibrational modes and nonadiabatic coupling between electronic states. Our simulations reveal that tr-QGS captures electronic coherence oscillating at 0.6 eV for ∼50 fs, a signature of nonadiabatic coupling that was obscured in time-resolved measurements. Moreover, we observe a direct transfer from electronic to vibrational coherence at 200 fs, providing real-time visualization of vibronic relaxation pathways. Photon entanglement eliminates background noise and ground-state bleaching artifacts, which plague time-resolved measurements. These results establish tr-QGS as a transformative tool for interrogating nonadiabatic dynamics in molecular aggregates, light-harvesting complexes, and photocatalysts, offering a route to reveal quantum coherence effects in chemistry with unprecedented precision.

title:
Aligned
Self-Assembled Nanostructure by Chemical Force
Trigger, Biased Migration, and Oscillatory Hydrogel Growth
content:
Abstract
Cells generate pico-to-nanonewton forces through metabolic circuits and diffusion for downstream processes, including stress fiber assembly and cellular growth. The inherent complexities of the system’s processing, reactivity, and adaptability make it difficult to recapitulate in a synthetic setting. Herein, we compartmentalized the urease-urea feedback-controlled reaction network (FCRN), demonstrating global vs local function adaptability by coupling with peptide self-assembly. Compartmentalized FCRN (c-FCRN) facilitates chemical energy-to-mechanical energy conversion, creating forces on the piconewton scale, allowing nanofiber alignment, akin to what a cell does. The trade-off between multiple microscale interactions in the chemo-material network implies molecular-biased migration resembling chemotactic-like directed motion in synthetic settings, which promotes spatial self-assembly remodelling. Consequently, regulating the reaction-diffusion chemistry, we demonstrate oscillatory hydrogel growth by encasing the c-FCRN with a physical membrane barrier. Furthermore, c-FCRN provides a rudimentary structure-building system to create various complex hydrogel structures, bypassing the 3D printing tools. Thus, the chemo-material network provides proof-of-concept for biomimetic material development by emulating biologically inspired technologies.

title:
Cisplatin Conjugated
with Vinylsulfonamide Cross-Links
Pyruvate Kinase M2 to Trigger Ferroptosis
content:
Abstract
Cisplatin serves as a first-line chemotherapeutic agent due to its DNA binding property. However, this intrinsic electrophilicity drives off-target interactions with proteins, which compromises anticancer efficacy, and also suggests the presence of unexplored targets. To identify platinum-binding proteins, a class of platinum(II) complexes containing a covalent vinylsulfonamide group were designed to provide stronger affinity for target engagement. By using competitive chemical proteomics technology, pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) was identified as the direct target of Pt1. The intracellular binding involved the recognition of the Cys49 pocket via cis-platinum moiety, which was strengthened by the synergistic event of platinum-centered ligand exchange and vinylsulfonamide-mediated covalent anchoring. This effective multimodal interaction disrupted PKM2 oligomerization and promoted its nuclear translocation. Subsequently, Pt1 induced ferroptosis via the PKM2-HMOX1 axis, further enhanced by mitochondrial oxidative stress. In xenograft models, Pt1 exhibited antitumor efficacy comparable to that of cisplatin, along with lower hepatotoxicity. This study presents a cisplatin conjugate that induces ferroptosis through intramolecular protein cross-linking, providing a synergistic coordination-covalent strategy for nonclassical platinum-based therapeutics.

title:
Comparing Nuclear Reaction
Coordinates Driving Photoinduced
Proton-Coupled Electron and Energy Transfer
content:
Abstract
Proton transfer is coupled to electron transfer or electronic excitation energy transfer in proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and proton-coupled energy transfer (PCEnT) reactions, respectively. Although photoinduced PCET and PCEnT have been studied extensively in anthracene–phenol–pyridine molecular triads, the nuclear reaction coordinates for these two pathways are still unknown. Herein, we identify the nuclear reaction coordinates for PCET and PCEnT in the triads by sampling the seam space between the relevant intersecting diabatic states. The reaction coordinate has contributions mainly from anthracene and phenol for PCET but involves the entire triad, including pyridine, for PCEnT. Both reaction coordinates involve motions related to contraction of the phenol C–O bond as well as motions within the anthracene rings that differ for PCET and PCEnT due to different charge distributions. The proton acceptor motion contributes more to the PCEnT than the PCET reaction coordinate. Both PCET and PCEnT reactions are concerted in that there is no stable intermediate, but they are both most likely asynchronous. Our analysis also suggests that PCET proceeds through a conical intersection in its minimum energy pathway, whereas PCEnT moves through an avoided crossing. The quantum mechanical treatment of the transferring proton within a vibronically nonadiabatic framework suggests that the kinetic isotope effect may be greater for PCEnT than for PCET, although more extensive calculations are required for confirmation. Understanding the fundamental similarities and differences between PCET and PCEnT mechanisms will help guide the design of proton-coupled systems that favor either charge transfer or energy transfer.

title:
Mechanistic
Insights of Electroreductive Cobalt-Catalyzed
Asymmetric Radical Addition
content:
Abstract
Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric electroreduction has emerged as a compelling platform for enantioselective C–C bond formation, with notable advances in electroreductive cross-coupling. Translating this success to stereocontrolled radical additions across unsaturated bonds remains a formidable challenge, particularly for the construction of fully substituted stereogenic carbon centers. Herein, we report an electroreductive, cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric radical addition of diverse organohalides to α-imino esters. This protocol delivers enantioenriched α-quaternary amino acid derivatives in up to 95% ee, completely circumventing the need for stoichiometric metal reductants. Beyond its synthetic utility, the electrochemical platform uniquely enables the direct interrogation of the operative electron-transfer events. A comprehensive mechanistic study─encompassing cyclic voltammetry, in situ electrochemical EPR spectroscopy, DFT calculations, stoichiometric experiments, and radical-trapping experiments─elucidates a highly orchestrated catalytic manifold. Crucially, we demonstrate that the α-imino ester serves a dual role, acting as both a radical acceptor and a redox-active ligand for the chiral cobalt catalyst. Subsequent cathodic reduction of the resulting cobalt–imine complex generates a key low-valent species that engages the alkyl halide via a turnover-limiting single-electron transfer (SET) to produce the requisite alkyl radical. Overall, this work establishes a robust electrochemical framework that synergizes reaction innovation with fundamental mechanistic elucidation in asymmetric radical catalysis.

title:
Amorphous Halide Cathodes
Enable 75C All-Solid-State
Lithium Batteries
content:
Abstract
Power delivery in all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) is often pursued by maximizing the bulk ionic conductivity of cathode active materials (CAMs), while grain-boundary (GB) ion-transport barriers caused by lattice mismatch remain a major kinetic bottleneck. Here, we reveal that minimizing GB transport barriers, rather than simply enhancing intrinsic conductivity, unlocks ultrafast ion-transport in halide CAMs. Amorphization converts crystalline LiVCl4 into a conformal amorphous phase that preserves short-range V–Cl coordination while minimizing long-range ion-transport tortuosity. Despite lower bulk Li+ conductivity, amorphous LiVCl4 dramatically reduces GB-associated interfacial resistance and enables a catholyte-free cathode (CAM content: 90 wt %) to deliver a capacity of 74.3 mAh g–1 at 5 mA cm–2, compared with 10.2 mAh g–1 for the crystalline counterpart. Meanwhile, the ASSLB further operates across a wide temperature range from −30 to 60 °C and achieves 84.2% capacity utilization at an ultrahigh A-LiVCl4 areal loading of 53.4 mg cm–2. Coupled with amorphous LiTaOCl4, the ASSLB achieves 102.1 mAh g–1 at 20 mA cm–2 (∼75C) and retains 82.3% capacity after 16,000 cycles. These results establish amorphization-enabled conformal interfaces as a new paradigm for ultrahigh-power ASSLBs.

title:
Harnessing Surface
Wrinkling Instability for Visualizing
Dynamic Chemistry in Polymer Networks
content:
Abstract
Studying dynamic chemical behaviors is fundamental to understanding and regulating the dynamic responses and functions of polymer materials. However, real-time, intuitive, and selective visualization of these molecular processes─particularly when multiple dynamic motifs coexist─remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce surface wrinkles as a visualization platform that directly translates dynamic chemical behaviors in polymers into observable macroscopic morphological changes. Using a dual-cross-linked polymer network (DCN) containing quadruple hydrogen bonds and mechanical bonds as a model system, we fabricate stable wrinkles via modulus mismatch in a bilayer architecture. In situ microscopy reveals that acid-triggered dissociation of quadruple hydrogen bonds causes rapid wrinkle erasure due to network disruption, whereas base-induced rotaxane sliding leads to gradual wrinkle erasure owing to network relaxation, reflecting their distinct dynamic mechanisms and time scales. Rheological analyses on single-cross-linked model networks corroborate these macroscopic observations at the molecular level. Moreover, by programming wrinkle patterns with “write–hide–read” functionality, we achieve macroscopic visualization and differentiation of microscopic dynamic processes. This work establishes surface wrinkling as a powerful and intuitive platform for real-time monitoring of dynamic chemistry and provides valuable insights for designing functional polymer materials with tunable macroscopic properties.

title:
General
Synthesis of Inverse Opal Covalent Organic
Framework Photonic Crystals
content:
Abstract
Constructing highly crystalline inverse opal covalent organic framework photonic crystals (IO COF PhCs) remains challenging due to the incompatibility between the spatial confinement required for inverse opal replication and the synthesis process of COFs. Inspired by the semi-solid chitin infiltration and confined solidification process in beetle photonic architectures, a solvent-free template-assisted melt pressing (STAMP) strategy is developed for the general synthesis of crystalline IO COF PhCs. The quasi-solid precursor state facilitates efficient template infiltration while remaining reactive for COF crystallization, affording ordered macroporous photonic architectures within 3 min. This strategy is broadly applicable to a library of 16 COFs spanning β-ketoenamine, hydrazone, imine, and imide linkages, yielding decimeter-scale monoliths with designable structural colors across the visible spectrum. By integrating periodic macroporosity, permanent framework porosity, and photonic functionality into one material platform, the resulting IO COF PhCs enable cross-scale programmable optical encoding and visually self-reporting adsorption. The application potential of IO COF PhCs is demonstrated for biomimetic anti-counterfeiting patterns and structural-color-indicated Au capture. This work establishes a general route toward crystalline IO COF PhCs and provides a versatile platform for coupling molecular functionality with photonic regulation in advanced smart materials.

title:
Macrocycle Size-Controlled
Dynamic and Static Chirality
in Donor–Acceptor [2]Catenanes
content:
Abstract
Chiral [2]catenanes, a prominent class of mechanically interlocked molecules (MIMs), can exhibit either static or dynamic mechanostereochemistry. Controlling these mechanostereochemical states without altering the covalent connectivity, however, remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of chiral [2]catenanes derived from ExBox and cycloparaphenyleneperylene (CPPP), whose dynamic behavior is altered by the size of the CPPP macrocycle. We identified a sharp, size-dependent threshold: The conformational stereogenic unit of [7]CPPP is kinetically locked, whereas those of [8]CPPP and [9]CPPP are dynamic at room temperature. This conformational stereochemistry strongly biases the co-conformational stereochemistry in the catenane, effectively resulting in a single dominant diastereomer. This effective coupling of the two stereogenic units allows the conformational stereochemistry to be biased by the ion pairing of the interlocked cationic ring with a chiral anion. This research highlights the potential of mechanically interlocked architectures for controlling the dynamic mechanostereochemistry.

title:
Fe-Incorporated
MoO 3  Nanorods as Efficient
Anodic Electrocatalysts for Urea-Assisted Alkaline and Seawater Oxidation
Reactions: Unraveling OER and UOR Interfacial Kinetics via Electrochemical
Impedance Spectroscopy and Distribution of Relaxation Times Analysis
content:
Abstract
Oxygen evolution reaction (OER), characterized by sluggish kinetics and high energy demand, remains a major bottleneck for large-scale hydrogen production, particularly under the challenging conditions of seawater electrolysis. Herein, Fe-incorporated MoO3 nanorods are successfully synthesized via a facile one-pot hydrothermal route, where the Fe content is systematically optimized to enhance electrocatalytic activity. Among the prepared catalysts, FeM15 exhibits superior performance toward both the OER and the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) in alkaline and natural seawater electrolytes. FeM15 achieves low OER overpotentials of 264 and 306 mV at 10 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH and seawater electrolytes, respectively, along with excellent long-term stability. Replacing OER with UOR significantly reduces the anodic energy requirement, lowering the operating potential by 148 mV in alkaline electrolyte and 184 mV in alkaline seawater. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analyses reveal that OER is governed by sluggish multistep interfacial processes, whereas UOR proceeds through accelerated charge-transfer kinetics with lower polarization resistance and relaxation time. Despite the complex ionic environment of seawater, urea-assisted electrolysis effectively mitigates kinetic limitations and substantially enhances anodic reaction efficiency. These findings highlight FeM15 as a promising and durable electrocatalyst for energy-efficient hydrogen production in both alkaline and seawater electrolysis systems.

title:
Numerical
Study on Multiphase Production Dynamics
and Sand Migration in Deepwater Unconsolidated Shallow Gas Reservoirs
with Hydrate-Bearing Layer
content:
Abstract
Deepwater shallow gas reservoirs possess substantial resource potential. However, because they are commonly hosted in unconsolidated sandstones and overlain by a hydrate-bearing layer (HBL), their development is accompanied by complex fluid–solid interactions and significant sand production risks. In this study, a three-dimensional radial multiphase and multicomponent numerical model incorporating sand migration was established using CMG STARS to investigate the production behavior and spatiotemporal evolution of gas, water, and sand during depressurization production of a shallow gas layer (SGL) beneath an HBL. The results show that gas, water, and sand production rates rapidly reach peak values at the early production stage. Thereafter, gas production gradually declines with reservoir pressure depletion, whereas the gradual restoration of water-phase mobility leads to a slow increase in water production rate and water–gas ratio. Hydrate dissociation remains limited to the gas–water interface, while the sand production zone evolves from rapid expansion to gradual contraction. increases in pore volume and flow capacity induced by sand migration contributes little to gas production enhancement, with a maximum increase of only 1.2%. Higher reservoir permeability results in greater gas and water production, a higher water–gas ratio, and higher sand production. In contrast, a higher initial water saturation of the SGL reduces gas production but increases water production and water–gas ratio while suppressing sand production. A larger overall pressure drawdown enhances gas and water productivity but aggravates sand production. A smaller single-step pressure reduction causes a more pronounced delay in productivity release and induces alternating expansion–contraction fluctuations of the sand production zone. These findings provide guidance for sand-control design and production optimization in deepwater shallow gas reservoirs.

title:
Interfacial
and Bulk Stabilization Mechanisms of Thermally
Stable anionic–zwitterionic Foam Fracturing Fluids for Unconventional-Reservoir
Applications
content:
Abstract
Foam fracturing fluids can reduce water consumption and improve proppant transport compared with conventional water-based fracturing fluids, but maintaining foam stability as temperature increases remains challenging because of accelerated drainage, film thinning, and bubble coalescence. This study aimed to develop and mechanistically evaluate thermally stable foam systems based on α-olefin sulfonate (AOS), sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS), and lauryl sulfobetaine (LB), with cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) included as a reference individual surfactant and AOS–LB and SDBS–LB investigated as binary mixtures. Interfacial and thermodynamic properties were characterized at 25 °C, while foam performance was evaluated at 30–70 °C. The mixed surfactant systems exhibited superior foam performance compared with the individual surfactants. AOS–LB showed a stronger tendency toward bulk micellization and drainage resistance, whereas SDBS–LB exhibited more favorable interfacial characteristics, bulk viscoelasticity, and the highest overall foam stability. At 70 °C, SDBS–LB maintained a foam half-life of 65 min and reduced proppant settling velocity by approximately 46% relative to AOS. The combined results revealed distinct but complementary stabilization pathways, with AOS–LB dominated by bulk structural organization and SDBS–LB benefiting from favorable interfacial characteristics and bulk viscoelasticity. The novelty of this work lies in establishing an integrated framework that relates interfacial characteristics, bulk rheology, drainage, bubble morphology, and proppant transport to the temperature-dependent stability of anionic–zwitterionic foam systems. These findings identify SDBS–LB as a promising formulation for further development of foam fracturing fluids for unconventional-reservoir applications.

title:
MXene-Integrated
Ni–Hf Nanoflowers for Efficient
Water Splitting in Alkaline Wastewater: Experimental and DFT Insights
content:
Abstract
Alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) is a promising technology for producing green hydrogen. Unfortunately, the requirements for purified water, costs, and current limitations restrict its application. We proposed solutions to these barriers by employing wastewater effluents and an efficient MXene-based model electrocatalyst (NiHf-LDH/MXene/NF). In a two-electrode cell configuration, it requires 1.89, 1.92, 1.95, and 1.98 V for deionized water (DI), tertiary effluent (TE), secondary effluent (SE) from an external membrane bioreactor (eMBR), and the activated sludge process (ASP) to attain 1000 mA/cm2, outperforming benchmark electrocatalysts (Pt/C∥IrO2). Durability was evaluated at 650 mA/cm2 for 200 h in wastewater effluent, with a 0.603 mV/h drop. The system’s energy efficiency was 71.7 and 60.5% (based on the lower heating value (LHV)) at 100 and 1000 mA/cm2, respectively. Moreover, pollutant levels decreased: chemical oxygen demand (COD) (47.2%), total nitrogen (TN) (49.7%), turbidity (53.8%), and total dissolved solids (TDS) (5.7%). Density functional theory (DFT) indicates that the model electrocatalyst features an excellent adsorption energy (0.51 eV) for water molecules, which favors electrochemical reactions.

title:
HEFA-Derived
Sustainable Aviation Fuel: A Review of
Catalytic Upgrading, Techno-economic Viability, and Machine Learning-Guided
Optimization
content:
Abstract
Commercial aviation contributes approximately 2% of global anthropogenic CO2 emissions, while non-CO2 effects, including nitrogen oxides (NOx), soot/black carbon particles, and contrail-induced cirrus formation, substantially increase the total climate impact. Hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids synthetic paraffinic kerosene (HEFA-SPK) remains the most commercially deployed ASTM-certified sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) pathway, reducing life-cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by approximately 55–92% on a CO2-equivalent basis relative to conventional Jet A-1, with variations driven by feedstock type, hydrogen source, and life-cycle assessment methodology and assumptions. However, large-scale HEFA-SAF deployment remains constrained by catalyst deactivation, limited jet-range selectivity, high hydrogen demand, and volatile lipid feedstock costs. Unlike previous HEFA-SAF reviews that evaluated catalyst development, process conversion, and economic assessment in isolation, this work provides a multiscale integration framework that systematically links molecular-level catalyst mechanisms with techno-economic performance and machine learning (ML) optimization. Within this framework, catalyst selectivity among the “hydrodeoxygenation” (HDO), “decarboxylation” (DCX), and “decarbonylation” (DCN) pathways is directly connected to hydrogen consumption and the feedstock-dependent minimum jet fuel selling price (MJFSP), whereas “hydrocracking” and “hydroisomerization” efficiency are linked to hydrogen costs and process configurations. Drawing on the literature from 2017 to June 2026, this review critically evaluates the opportunities and limitations of ML across the HEFA-SAF value chain, emphasizing that ML-guided catalyst discovery requires rigorous experimental validation before industrial implementation. To address data fragmentation across the published literature, a standardized, integrated HEFA data set framework─combining catalyst-level descriptors, process-level parameters, techno-economic indicators and a 2025–2030 research roadmap─is introduced as the primary contribution. The roadmap identifies four critical priorities: extending catalyst lifetime under realistic feeds, reducing external hydrogen dependence, establishing reliable low-cost feedstock supply chains, and developing validated data sets for ML-driven optimization. By establishing explicit linkages across catalytic science, process engineering, techno-economic analysis, and data-driven tools, this review accelerates cost-competitive and scalable HEFA-SAF deployment.

title:
Carbon Pore
Architecture for Sulfur Accommodation,
Retention, and Electrochemical Kinetics in Lithium–Sulfur Cells
content:
Abstract
Lithium–sulfur cells provide an ideal platform for studying how carbon pore architecture governs sulfur accommodation, polysulfide retention, and electrochemical kinetics. Although porous carbons with different pore characteristics have been investigated, their intrinsic pore-structure effects remain difficult to distinguish because previous studies generally employ independently synthesized carbons with different surface chemistries and morphologies. Here, we establish an experimental platform by systematically blending commercial porous carbons with controlled pore architectures while preserving their intrinsic physicochemical properties. Dynamic image analysis, gas adsorption, electron microscopy, elemental mapping, and thermogravimetric analysis reveal systematic changes in pore structure, particle morphology, sulfur distribution, and sulfur retention as the carbon ratio is varied. Sulfur confined within micropore-dominated structures exhibits greater thermal stability than sulfur accommodated in mesopore-dominated structures, demonstrating that sulfur accommodation and sulfur retention are fundamentally different processes. Electrochemical measurements further establish a clear structure–property relationship, showing that micropore-dominated architectures enhance sulfur retention but impede ion transport, whereas mesopore-dominated architectures facilitate reaction kinetics at the expense of sulfur confinement and electrode stability. An optimized pore architecture balances these competing effects, enabling efficient sulfur utilization, suppressed polysulfide migration, improved reaction kinetics, and stable cycling under high sulfur loading. As a result, this study provides mechanistic insight and practical design principles for rational pore-architecture engineering in lithium–sulfur cells.

title: Capacity–Retention Balance Determines Single-Crystal Payoff in Ni-Rich Cathodes
content:
Abstract
Single crystallization is widely pursued to mitigate structural degradation in Ni-rich layered cathodes, yet its practical value remains difficult to define because improved durability can be accompanied by kinetic limitations and an initial-capacity penalty. Here, we establish a literature-derived quantitative framework that converts this long-standing trade-off into a measurable payoff criterion. Directly comparable polycrystalline–single-crystal cathode pairs from 12 datasets and 42 test contexts were evaluated through logarithmic response ratios describing initial-capacity, retention, and end-of-test capacity effects. Single-crystal cathodes showed higher retention in 67% of comparisons but higher initial capacity in only 19%, while 64% ultimately achieved a higher end-of-test capacity. These results identify compensation between early capacity sacrifice and durability gain as the central determinant of single-crystal benefit. Cross-dataset analysis further shows that this payoff is condition-dependent. The resulting break-even framework shifts single crystallization from a qualitative stability preference to a quantitative materials selection principle and offers a broader strategy for evaluating energy-storage materials in which long-term durability is gained at the expense of initial performance.

title: Design of Porphyrin-Based 2D Covalent Organic Frameworks and 2D/2D Heterojunctions for Enhanced Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
content:
Abstract
Photocatalytic water splitting is a promising approach to sustainable green hydrogen (H2) production by harnessing solar energy. Among emerging photocatalysts, two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have attracted significant interest because of their crystallinity, stability, and porosity. COFs offer an effective strategy to tune optoelectronic properties by rationally selecting organic linkers, thereby improving water-splitting performance. In this context, porphyrin-based 2D COFs offer an optimal band structure and excellent light-harvesting properties crucial for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. Herein, we report three porphyrin-based COFs, ZnP-TP, ZnP-BT, and ZnP-TZ, designed by strategically selecting organic linkers. Among them, ZnP-TZ exhibits the highest hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) rate of 34 mmol g–1 h–1. To further enhance HER performance, we fabricated ZnP-TZ COF/g-C3N4 heterojunctions. The optimized heterostructure, g-C3N4/ZnP-TZ (CN-TZ-2) with a 1:2 composition, achieved an HER rate of ∼70 mmol g–1 h–1, twice that of pristine COF. Comprehensive spectroscopic and electrochemical studies revealed a synergistic COF/g-C3N4 interaction that facilitated charge separation and interfacial transfer, suppressed recombination, and enhanced photocatalytic HER. This study highlights the significance of 2D–2D heterostructure materials and provides innovative direction for rational design of efficient photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen generation.

title: Microenvironment-Directed Product Selectivity in Electrochemical C–N Coupling: Recent Advancements and Future Outlook
content:
Abstract
The C–N bond is integral to essential agronomical, biochemical, and industrial products, including urea, amides, amines, amino acids, oximes, and pharmaceuticals. Whereas traditional synthesis demands costly noble metals, extreme temperatures, and high pressures that generate toxic pollution, electrocatalytic C–N coupling provides a highly selective, green alternative powered by renewable electricity under ambient conditions. By co-reducing abundant feedstocks like CO2, CO, N2, and NOx, this method tackles the profound thermodynamic barriers of breaking robust N≡N and C=O bonds. Nevertheless, the simultaneous reduction of carbon and nitrogen introduces severe kinetic hurdles, notably mismatched intermediate reaction rates and aggressive competing side reactions. Overcoming these barriers requires highly stable catalysts operating at low potentials, coupled with rigorous microenvironment engineering adapted from mature CO2 and NOx/N2 reduction systems. By precisely shaping mass transport, reactant coverage, and local electric fields, selectivity is maximized through three primary strategies: targeted catalyst design utilizing defect engineering, ligand coordination, and nanoscale morphological control across single-atom, single-metal, and bimetallic architectures; dynamic pulsed electrolysis; and electrolyte tuning via pH and cation modifications. By comprehensively evaluating these catalytic innovations, substrate activation mechanisms, characterization techniques, and integrated electrolytic cell configurations, this review provides a definitive roadmap for translating laboratory-scale organonitrogen electrosynthesis into sustainable, large-scale industrial manufacturing through microenvironment tuning.

title: Br-Related Local Structural Dynamics Associated with Reversible Photovoltaic Evolution in Mixed-Halide Perovskite Solar Cells Revealed via Br K-Edge X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy
content:
Abstract
The microscopic origin of photovoltaic performance evolution in mixed-halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains unclear because direct observation of element-specific local structural evolution has been limited. In this study, the relationship between photovoltaic performance and local halide structural evolution was investigated via Br K-edge and I L3-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy. Br K-edge spectral features exhibited systematic changes during repeated measurement/storage cycles that correlated strongly with normalized photovoltaic performance. Composition-dependent analysis revealed that the correlation between Br-related spectral evolution and photovoltaic performance was the strongest at an intermediate Br content (35% Br), whereas no comparable composition dependence was observed in the I L3-edge response. A state-transition model is hypothesized to describe the relationship between local Br structural evolution and photovoltaic performance evolution. These results demonstrate that photovoltaic performance evolution is more closely associated with Br-related local structural evolution than with I-related spectral changes, providing critical insights into the microscopic processes associated with photovoltaic performance evolution in mixed-halide PSCs.

title: Fast and Selective Photochemical Doping of Spiro‐OMeTAD
content:
Sixty seconds of UV light converts spiro‐OMeTAD into its clean +1/+2 oxidized states while >98% of lithium is extracted into an aqueous phase by 12‐crown‐4. Proton‐tunable hydroxyl‐radical chemistry generates oxidants whose reduction potentials bracket the spiro2+/spiro3+ couple, providing thermodynamic oxidation‐state selectivity, as quantified by DFT.








ABSTRACT
Oxidizing a redox‐active molecule rapidly and selectively to a targeted oxidation state, without residual dopant ions, is a central challenge in molecular doping. Spiro‐OMeTAD exemplifies it: the standard LiTFSI/O2 protocol is slow (>12 h), leaves hygroscopic Li+ aggregates in the film, and yields an uncontrolled +1/+2/+3 mixture. Here we report a biphasic photochemical doping platform, the crown ether/acid‐assisted doping system (CEADS), in which a chlorobenzene solution of spiro‐OMeTAD/LiTFSI is layered above an aqueous phase of concentrated HCl and 12‐crown‐4 (12C4) and irradiated with broadband UV. Doping completes in 60 s, yielding a > 104‐fold conductivity enhancement (σ = 1.18 × 10−2 S cm−1, ≈60‐fold over LiTFSI/O2) and removing >98% of Li+ from the organic phase. Three sequentially optimized parameters control the spiro‐OMeTAD oxidation manifold: high H+ quenches over‐oxidation, Cl− provides secondary kinetic modulation at intermediate acid, and 4 equiv 12C4 enforces charge‐balanced phase transfer. Temperature‐dependent conductivity yields an Arrhenius activation energy Ea = 0.19 eV (R2 = 0.99) over 193–298 K, consistent with reduced Li‐related deep traps. CEADS produces lithium‐free, cleanly +1/+2‐oxidized hole‐transport films on a minute timescale.

title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Silver Icosahedrons for SERS Sensing Applications
content:
We demonstrate an electrochemical strategy for fabricating Ag icosahedrons via kinetically controlled growth, achieved through the engineering of both the cathode and the electrolyte. By simply tuning the deposition potential, current, or electrolyte composition, hierarchical Ag icosahedrons with tunable architectures can be produced. These hierarchical structures exhibit excellent potential as surface‐enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) substrates. We open up an electrochemical approach towards metastable microparticles inaccessible by other methods.








ABSTRACT
Ag icosahedrons, characterized by the size‐dependent distribution of strain fields, has garnered increasing interests across disciplines from crystallography to materials science. However, the metastability arising from such intrinsic strain greatly restricts the available synthetic routes. Here, we present a facile aqueous‐phase electrodeposition technique for the robust synthesis of Ag icosahedrons. By decreasing the Ag reduction rate, we achieve enhanced control over the electrodeposition kinetics, as quantitatively evidenced by the apparent activation energy. The pronounced kinetic stability allows for the synthesis of particles up to 5 µm in size within 10 min (Pretreatment time: 48 h). Through systematic variation of applied potentials, currents, and electrolyte compositions, we enable the design of Ag icosahedrons with tunable hierarchical structures. These structured particles can be effectively employed as surface‐enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) substrates for pesticide detection. This work establishes a stable and pure model system that facilitates the straightforward synthesis of metastable structures.

title: Cation Vacancy‐Modulated NiOOH for Electro‐Oxidative Alcohol Dehydrogenation and Amide Synthesis Coupled With Hydrogen Evolution
content:
The cationic vacancy induces the high‐valent nickel (Ni4+) generation and inhibits the poisoning of Ni sites by NH3, while the activated lattice oxygen enhances the rate of anodic oxidative coupling of benzyl alcohol and NH3 to achieve the efficient productivity of benzamide coupling with cathodic hydrogen production in the whole reaction.








ABSTRACT
Utilizing thermodynamically favorable biomass conversion to replace oxygen evolution reactions (OER) can achieve efficient H2 production under low energy consumption. However, this strategy has seldom been studied in the electrosynthesis of C–N oxidative coupling reactions (COR), mainly due to the challenge of simultaneously achieving efficient oxidation and coupling reaction. Herein, an electrochemical etching strategy was employed to prepare a V+‐NiOOH catalyst rich in cation vacancies (V+), which succeeded in the electrosynthesis of benzamide from benzyl alcohol (BA) and NH3 at 1.50 V versus RHE, with 86% selectivity and 100% conversion. Synchrotron radiation analysis confirmed that the presence of V+ promoted the generation of high‐valent Ni4+(t2g6 eg0) species and activated the lattice oxygen in Ni4+‐Olat‐Ni3+. Related in situ characterization and theoretical calculations explained the significant role of Ni4+‐Olat‐O∙ in catalyzing the oxidation of O–H and C–H bonds, and the dynamic reconstruction between Ni3+ and Ni4+ inhibited the poisoning effect of NH3 on the catalyst. Notably, by coupling with cathodic H2 production, an amide yield of 0.81 mmol h−1 was achieved under 200 mA, and the H2 production energy consumption was reduced by 24.1%. It provides important guidance for promoting green and efficient utilization of resources and energy.

title: Rapid Flow Synthesis of Zr‐MOF Nanoparticles in Supercritical CO2 for Toxic Chemical Removal
content:
Supercritical CO2 continuous‐flow synthesis produces highly crystalline Zr‐MOFs with residence times as short as 75 s. The resulting UiO‐66 and UiO‐66‐NH2 exhibit high porosity and effective adsorption and degradation of toxic chemicals.








ABSTRACT
Zirconium‐based metal‐organic frameworks (Zr‐MOFs) are promising materials for the adsorption and degradation of toxic chemicals; however, their scalable synthesis is hindered by the slow formation of Zr–oxo clusters. Here, we report rapid flow synthesis of Zr‐MOF nanoparticles in supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO2). Using UiO‐66 as a model system, we observe fast particle formation (17 s) and achieve 54% ± 0.28% yield in 75 s with an averaged BET surface area of 1274 ± 38 m2g−1. Possible contributing factors to the fast nucleation include reduced solvent polarity, fast mass transfer, and modulated solute miscibility with the scCO2/DMF medium. Acid modulators appear to be critical for regulating Zr‐oxo cluster formation and the morphological transition from nanoparticle aggregates to single crystals. This strategy is extended to the synthesis of high‐quality UiO‐66‐NH2 and MOF‐808. Products of the rapidly synthesized UiO series were evaluated for chemical warfare agent (CWA) simulant decomposition and TICs adsorption. UiO‐66‐NH2 showed faster DMNP hydrolysis and higher NH3, Cl2, and CK uptake than UiO‐66, with performance comparable to MOFs produced by days‐long batch synthesis.

title: Solvated‐Electron‐Driven Intercalation Enables Electron‐Rich KxNbS2 Construction and Exfoliation
content:
A molten‐salt solvated‐electron strategy enables electron injection into transition metal dichalcogenides. Coupling electron transfer with alkali cation intercalation generates an electron‐rich intermediate without relying on intrinsic cationic frameworks. This electron‐rich state facilitates solvent‐dependent exfoliation pathways, providing a route to modulate the electronic and structural properties of two‐dimensional materials for advanced applications.








ABSTRACT
While creating electron‐rich states can tune material properties, achieving this in van der Waals (vdW) materials lacking cationic frameworks remains challenging. Here, we report a molten‐salt solvated‐electron strategy that injects electrons into the vdW gaps of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs). Using a Ga‐KCl system, we construct an electron‐rich intermediate KxNbS2 (x≤0.5), wherein coupled K+ intercalation provides charge compensation and drives superlattice formation. Spectroscopic characterization confirm electron injection and partial reduction of the host lattice. This state enables solvent‐dependent exfoliation, protic solvents drive a chemical pathway, whereas aprotic solvents facilitate physical delamination via electrostatic repulsion. Demonstrating applicability across TMDCs (NbS2, TaS2, NbSe2 and WS2), alkali salts, and electron donors, this strategy provides a route to engineer the electronic structures and interlayer interactions of two‐dimensional (2D) materials for catalysis and quantum applications.

title: Symmetry‐Breaking Polarized Ir‐COFs With Ultralow Exciton Binding Energy Enable Directional Charge Allocation for Synergistic Photocatalytic Gold Recovery and BPA Photodegradation
content:
A molecular‐induced polarization symmetry‐breaking strategy constructs a polarized iridium‐functionalized covalent organic framework with π–d–π* orbital coupling, creating a built‐in electric field, ultralow exciton binding energy (24.7 meV), and directional charge allocation. This suppresses charge crosstalk and enables synergistic photocatalytic gold recovery and bisphenol A degradation with mutual promotion, achieving 99.4% BPA removal and 3145 mg g−1 Au uptake.








ABSTRACT
Synergistic photocatalytic precious metal recovery and organic pollutant degradation promise sustainable resource recovery. However, this process is constrained by high exciton binding energy and disordered carrier migration, inducing charge crosstalk and sluggish kinetics among competing redox centers. A molecular induced polarization symmetry‐breaking (MIP‐SB) strategy constructs a polarized Ir‐functionalized covalent organic framework (COF), BT‐mBpyCN2+‐Ir, where Ir coordination creates a π–d–π* coupled electronic structure promoting directional ligand‐to‐ligand charge transfer (LLCT) for efficient charge allocation. This structural design generates a built‐in electric field, with Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) showing a surface potential of 120 mV. This strong internal field yields an ultralow exciton binding energy of 24.7 meV and a prolonged carrier lifetime of 1.85 ns. This directional charge allocation enables a mutual promotion effect: the bisphenol A (BPA) degradation rate constant increases by 21‐fold in the presence of Au(III), while the Au(III) reduction rate is enhanced by 3.8‐fold when BPA co‐exists. Consequently, under sacrificial‐agent‐free conditions, BT‐mBpyCN2+‐Ir achieves 99.4% BPA degradation within 30 min and a gold extraction capacity of 3145 mg g−1. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that BPA coexistence lowers the Gibbs free energy for Au(III)‐to‐Au(0) conversion, revealing a thermodynamically favored dual‐channel synergistic mechanism.

title: Molecularly Induced Carrier‐Polarity Regulation Enables Efficient Methylammonium‐Free Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
Spatially organized PBAC regulates carrier polarity in MA‐free wide‐bandgap perovskites by shifting the Fermi level toward the valence band and reducing the Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite energetic offset from 0.33 to 0.06 eV. Improved interfacial alignment promotes hole extraction and suppresses loss pathways, enabling a power‐conversion efficiency of 24.66%.








ABSTRACT
Methylammonium (MA)‐free wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskites are attractive top‐cell absorbers for tandem photovoltaics. However, defect‐related donor‐state contributions can shift the perovskite Fermi level away from the valence‐band maximum (VBM), creating an unfavorable energetic mismatch with the hole‐selective Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite contact and contributing to voltage and fill‐factor losses in perovskite solar cells with an inverted structure. Here, we introduce 4‐(piperidin‐4‐yl)benzoic acid hydrochloride (PBAC) as a spatially organized molecular additive that regulates the carrier polarity of MA‐free WBG perovskites while passivating defects. PBAC shifts the Fermi level toward the VBM and reduces the Fermi‐level offset at the Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite interface. This carrier‐polarity regulation improves energetic compatibility at the hole‐selective contact, facilitating hole extraction and suppressing interfacial recombination. Defect passivation and strain relaxation further inhibit halide migration and stabilize the mixed‐halide lattice. As a result, MA‐free WBG perovskite solar cells with bandgaps of 1.66 and 1.77 eV achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 24.66% and 20.74%, respectively. The unencapsulated PBAC‐treated 1.66 eV device retains 86% of its initial PCE after 1000 h of continuous AM 1.5G operation in ambient air. These results establish molecularly induced carrier‐polarity regulation as an effective strategy for reducing interfacial losses in MA‐free WBG perovskite solar cells.

title: Descriptor‐Guided Stabilization of Reconstructed Active Phases for High‐Activity and Durable CO2‐to‐Formate Conversion
content:
Electronic‐structure descriptors reveal an optimal partially reconstructed SnxOy/Sn interface for selective CO2‐to‐formate conversion. Amorphous SnO2 stabilizes this dynamic active phase, suppresses deep reduction and competing hydrogen evolution, and enables a formate partial current density of 438.0 mA cm−2 in a flow cell, offering a route to durable electrocatalysis.








ABSTRACT
Sn oxides are promising CO2RR electrocatalysts for formate production, but their high activity is difficult to sustain because cathodic reconstruction can over‐reduce active oxide‐derived surfaces to metallic Sn. This dynamic evolution makes it challenging to identify and stabilize the true working‐state active phase. Here, we construct a descriptor‐guided framework that links dynamic Sn‐oxide reconstruction with electronic‐structure evolution and formate‐producing activity to identify and stabilize the favorable working‐state active phase. Electronic‐structure analysis shows that the optimal SnxOy/Sn surface stabilizes the *OCHO intermediate through coupled charge‐polarization redistribution and Sn 5s/5p orbital modulation. To quantify this effect, we develop a TD descriptor integrating Bader charge, Sn 5p coupling, and Sn 5s lone‐pair activation, which exhibits a volcano‐type correlation with the limiting free energy, with the minimum at TD = 0.67 corresponding to the most favorable reconstructed SnxOy/Sn surface. Guided by this descriptor, amorphous SnO2 is designed to stabilize the favorable SnxOy/Sn working state and suppress deep reduction, achieving an HCOO− partial current density of 438.0 mA cm−2 at −1.8 V vs. RHE, 1.8 times that of commercial SnO2. This work provides a descriptor‐guided strategy for stabilizing reconstructed active phases in CO2RR.

title: Redirecting Bond Cleavage in Sacrificial Prelithiation via Dual‐Side Separator Engineering for Anode‐Free Lithium Batteries
content:
Multiscale failure mechanisms in AFLMBs versus the synergistic design of the dual‐side functionalized separator. To mitigate active‐lithium depletion and rampant dendritic growth, the dual‐functional separator synergizes cathode‐side catalytic prelithiation for lithium replenishment with anode‐side desolvation acceleration and in situ LiF‐rich SEI construction.









ABSTRACT
Anode‐free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) promise extreme gravimetric and volumetric energy densities but suffer from irreversible active lithium loss, sluggish desolvation kinetics, and dendritic proliferation. Herein, we report a catalyst‐induced bond‐cleavage redirection concept to unlock efficient sacrificial prelithiation, implemented via a dual‐side functionalized separator. On the cathode side, a 5 µm MoC1‐x/NC‐0.3Co coating redirects Li2C2O4 decomposition from high‐barrier Li–O cleavage to preferential C─C bond scission. Theoretical calculations and operando characterizations confirm this mechanistic shift, lowering the delithiation potential to 3.79 V at 60°C with a 99.5% Li+ utilization rate. To safeguard the liberated lithium inventory against depletion, the anode side integrates a PSSLi‐PFPE bilayer. This coating accelerates Li+ desolvation and drives the in‐situ construction of a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase, enabling Li symmetric cells cycling for over 1700 h (1.0 mAh cm−2, DOD = 80.7%). Bridging fundamental bond kinetics with practical engineering, the assembled 1.0 Ah anode‐free pouch cell (NCM811||MoC1‐x/NC‐0.3Co‐LCO/PE/PSSLi‐PFPE||Cu) achieves gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 458.6 Wh kg−1 and 1005.2 Wh L−1, a power output of 989.1 W kg−1, retaining 80.1% capacity after 100 cycles. This non‐invasive separator strategy provides a unified framework connecting bond kinetics to practical cell manufacturing, charting a feasible avenue for high‐energy AFLMBs.

title: Suppressing Photooxidation and Iodine Migration in HTL‐Free Carbon‐Based Perovskite Solar Cells via a Tailor‐Made Redox Guard
content:
A tailor‐made molecular guard is introduced to tackle both light‐induced oxidation and iodine migration in hole transport layer‐free carbon‐based perovskite solar cells. The guard works through multiple protective mechanisms, enabling a record efficiency of 19.96% with excellent long‐term stability. The strategy is further validated in Cs0.17FA0.83PbI3, delivering an efficiency of 20.70%.








ABSTRACT
Hole transport layer‐free carbon‐based perovskite solar cells (HTL‐free C‐PSCs) suffer rapid performance decay under operational stressors, driven by iodine migration and photogenerated superoxide radicals (O2•−). To break this photo‐oxidation‐iodine migration vicious cycle, we design a multifunctional molecular stabilizer, tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl)tetrathiafulvalene (4B‐TTF). This tailor‐made “molecular guard” works via two synergistic mechanisms: its reversible TTF core acts as a charge‐transfer mediator, reducing I2 to I− and scavenging O2•−, while four peripheral benzoic acid groups anchor to undercoordinated Pb2+ sites, passivating grain‐boundary defects. Incorporating 4B‐TTF into MAPbI3‐based devices yields a champion power‐conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.96%, vs. 17.58% for the control, by suppressing non‐radiative recombination. Unencapsulated devices retain 96.4% of their initial efficiency after 1200 h under ambient storage and 93.5% after 120 h under harsh UV‐oxygen exposure; encapsulated devices retain 90.32% after 700 h of continuous maximum power point (MPP) tracking under 1‐sun illumination at 55°C in nitrogen. The strategy is further validated in Cs0.17FA0.83PbI3 systems, delivering a state‐of‐the‐art PCE of 20.70%. This work provides a unified molecular‐level strategy to concurrently address ionic, radical, and defect‐related degradation, bridging the performance gap between low‐cost HTL‐free devices and conventional high‐cost architectures.
