title: Simultaneous Optimization of Thermoelectric Transport and Mechanical Performance in Full‐Zintl CaCd2Sb2/Mg3Sb2 Thermoelectric Modules
content:
By alloying with Na‐doped EuMg2Sb2, we realize synergistic band convergence, phonon scattering, and solid‐solution strengthening in CaCd2Sb2‐based Zintl phases. The optimized sample achieves a peak zT of ∼ 1.4 at 750 K, alongside improved mechanical robustness. After integration with Mg3Sb2‐based legs, the resulting full‐Zintl module exhibits a conversion efficiency approaching 11% under a temperature difference of 422 K.








ABSTRACT
Achieving both high thermoelectric performance and robust mechanical strength remains a key pursuit for the practical deployment of thermoelectric applications. Herein, a solid‐solution approach is employed in CaCd2Sb2 via alloying with EuMg2Sb2, achieving a synergistic optimization of electrical and phonon transport and mechanical performance. The incorporation of EuMg2Sb2 facilitates band degeneracy, thereby substantially improving the electrical transport properties. Together with the reduced thermal conductivity, the optimized composition exhibits a peak zT of ∼ 1.4 at 750 K and an average zT of ∼ 0.81 between 300 and 750 K. Furthermore, solid‐solution strengthening markedly enhances the mechanical properties, thereby ensuring mechanical integrity for reliable device integration. Leveraging transient liquid phase bonding, a 2 × 2 full‐Zintl module combining this optimized p‐type material with Mg3Sb2‐based n‐type legs achieves a conversion efficiency of ∼ 11% at a temperature difference of 422 K. This work highlights the viability of Zintl phases toward high‐efficiency thermoelectric modules.

title: Bifunctional Additive Enabled Thermoresponsive Electrolytes With Dual‐Mode Manipulation Toward Safe Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
A high volume fraction of vinylene carbonate‐based thermoresponsive electrolyte regulated by LiNO3 as a bifunctional additive (HVCE‐N) is proposed for safe lithium metal batteries. At ambient temperature, LiNO3 modifies the solvation structure and builds a Li3N/LiNxOy‐rich solid electrolyte interface for high‐rate performance. At high temperature, LiNO3 can regulate polymerization to enable steady operation up to 100°C and prevent thermal runaway at 200°C.








ABSTRACT
Thermal safety issues arising from electrolyte instability at elevated temperatures pose a critical challenge for lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs). Thermoresponsive electrolytes offer a promising solution, yet battery systems with high‐rate capability and reliable thermal protection have not been realized. Herein, we introduce a bifunctional LiNO3 additive into a high‐volume‐fraction vinylene carbonate‐based thermoresponsive electrolyte (HVCE‐N) to enhance the performance of LMBs at room and elevated temperatures. Notably, the introduction of the LiNO3 additive modifies the solvation structure of Li+ and forms a Li3N/LiNxOy solid electrolyte interface with high ionic conductivity. Under thermal shock, HVCE‐N undergoes a rapid liquid‐to‐solid phase transition upon free radical polymerization to form a polymer network. More importantly, LiNO3 can regulate the free radical concentration to control the degree of polymerization, thereby preserving high ion transport capability even after phase transition. As a result, a Li||NCM811 cell based on HVCE‐N exhibits high‐rate performance from 1C to 10C, and stable cycling at 100°C. When subjected to a thermal shock of 200°C, HVCE‐N suppresses thermal runaway for Li||NCM811 pouch cell. This electrolyte design offers a new strategy to develop highly safe LMBs with high‐rate performance.

title: Chloride‐Mediated Activation of Aluminum‐Alloyed Liquid Metal Anodes for Stretchable Asymmetric Energy Storage
content:
A gallium‐centered cell pairs an aluminum‐alloyed GaIn anode with a GaOOH cathode in a chloride‐rich water‐in‐ionic‐liquid electrolyte. Chlorogallate ions dissolve the native oxide that normally seals the liquid metal, and preferentially reduce indium seeds to oxide‐free clusters on which gallium plates and strips reversibly. The stretchable cell delivers 66.28 mWh cm−3 and 90% retention over 4000 cycles.








ABSTRACT
Gallium‐based liquid metals are attractive anodes for stretchable energy storage because they operate dendrite‐free, yet their bulk faradaic capacity remains locked behind a native oxide shell that conventional electrolytes cannot remove. Here, this passivation problem is resolved through the co‐design of an aluminum‐alloyed gallium–indium (AlGaIn) anode and a chloride‐rich water‐in‐ionic‐liquid (WIL) electrolyte, and the indium‐assisted electrochemical activation mechanism connecting them is identified. Al alloying converts the native oxide into a hydroxyl‐rich mixed Al–Ga–O shell susceptible to [GaCl4]−‐mediated etching, while the In(III) ions preferentially reduced into metallic patches that seed reversible Ga alloying/dealloying within the WIL. Potential‐resolved ex situ XPS indicates that in conventional TFSI‐based electrolytes, the electrode passivates beneath a TFSI‐derived interphase, whereas in the WIL, a chloride‐dominated electrode–electrolyte interphase forms instead. The activated anode gains 60% capacity during activation and retains ∼100% capacity over 1600 cycles at 500 mA g−1. Paired with a sonochemically derived GaOOH nanosheet cathode in a stretchable asymmetric cell, the asymmetric full cell delivers a maximum of 66.28 mWh cm−3 normalized to the active‐electrode volume, and 90% capacity retention over 4000 cycles. The halide‐mediated oxide‐displacement principle established here provides a generalizable electrolyte‐design strategy for oxide‐passivated liquid‐metal and post‐lithium anodes.

title: Homogenizing Fullerene Contacts by Supramolecular Host–Guest Assembly for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
In this work, we report a host–guest supramolecular strategy to homogenize fullerene electron transport layers. TPC spatially isolates PCBM molecules and forms a supramolecular network to supramolecularly stabilize them, inhibiting thermally induced aggregation. The optimized interface yields inverted PSCs with 26.83% PCE and 92.3% retention after 1000 h of 85°C MPPT.








ABSTRACT
Fullerene and its derivatives are widely adopted as electron transport layers (ETLs) in high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, fullerene materials are prone to aggregation and rearrangement under environmental stress, which acts as one of the critical factors restricting the long‐term operational stability of devices. Here, we report a host–guest supramolecular assembly strategy using rigid triptycene (TPC) molecules to stabilize fullerene‐based ETLs. The [6,6]‐phenyl‐C61‐butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM)–TPC host–guest interaction enables the spatial isolation and noncovalent immobilization of PCBM cages, which suppresses the thermal‐driven aggregation, crystallization, and morphological variation of PCBM layers. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.83%, with 96.0% efficiency retention after 1000 h of 85°C thermal aging and 92.3% retention after 1000 h of 85°C photothermal maximum power point tracking. This work offers a supramolecular solution for high‐stability optoelectronic devices.

content:
Abstract
The Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reaction is a cornerstone of C–C bond formation. However, heteroaryl boronic acids such as pyridyl and quinolyl derivatives remain challenging nucleophiles due to facile protodeboronation. Strategies enabling these substrates are limited to C(sp2)–C(sp2) formation. Efficient and modular C(sp2)–C(sp3) cross-coupling methods that directly employ these substrates remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a cross-organoboron platform that enables direct C(sp2)–C(sp3) bond formation from heteroaryl and alkyl organoboron reagents under visible-light irradiation using Ag2O/TiO2 nanoparticles (NPs). The two organoboron reagents undergo distinct Ag2O NP activations: alkyl boronates undergo single-electron photo-oxidation to generate alkyl radicals while arylboronates undergo transmetalation. Importantly, this method tolerates protodeboronation-prone pyridyl, quinolyl, α-heteroaryl boronic acids, and (hetero)aryl halide-containing substrates, including aryl iodides. High-throughput evaluation across 161 pharmaceutically relevant organoboron substrates identified 113 detectable couplings, and representative examples were validated at preparative scale. This work establishes photochemical cross-organoboron coupling as a complementary approach to classical transition-metal-catalyzed coupling and expands the accessible chemical space of heteroaryl organoboron reagents.

title:
Micelles as a Confined
Liquid: Standard and Two-Dimensional
Kinetics of Solute Rotation in Surfactant Micelles
content:
Abstract
The dynamics inside a surfactant micelle show clear confinement effects: solute rotation slows and develops a nonexponential relaxation. Multiple rate constants─rate dispersion─must be involved. These effects have been widely attributed to solutes confined to an outer layer of strongly ordered hydrocarbon chains, a layer similar to a Langmuir-Blodgett film. In this picture, confinement effects result from a surface phenomenon enhanced by the high surface area of a nanometer-sized particle. This paper presents results that are inconsistent with strong chain ordering. Varying the solute shows that most of the confinement-induced slowing is at the center of the micelle, not near its surface. Two-dimensional (two-relaxation-period) kinetics show that rate dispersion is mostly due to rate heterogeneity among different solute molecules. A homogeneous component of the stretched dynamics is also identified and is attributed to the coupling of the solute rotation with conformational relaxation of the hydrocarbon chains. In a picture consistent with these results, the micelle is unstructured, and the solutes are more widely distributed than in the conventional model. Confinement effects are not due to surface effects; they are due to the clash in the lengths of the hydrocarbon chain and the particle diameter. This study is enabled by a nonparametric, “data-first” approach that enhances the interpretation of kinetics, especially two-dimensional kinetics.

title:
Hierarchically Structured
Anti-Perovskite Oxynitride-Hydride
Enabling Ammonia Synthesis via a Cooperative Mechanism Mediated by
(N 2 ) −  Ions
content:
Abstract
Ba3AlO4-xNyHz with an antiperovskite structure is employed as a support for transition-metal catalysts for ammonia synthesis. This metastable material is synthesized by employing multiple anions with different valences and ionic radii. The optimized non-noble metal catalyst, Co(5.8 wt %)/Ba3AlO4-xNyHz/Al2O3, exhibits an exceptional ammonia synthesis rate of 15.9 mmol g–1 h–1 at 0.9 MPa and 300 °C, outperforming benchmark Cs–Ru/MgO, industrial Fe catalyst, and recently reported non-noble metal catalysts. Structural analyses show that Ba3AlO4-xNyHz and Co species self-organize on γ-Al2O3 nanorods to form a hierarchically structured catalyst. Combined experimental and density functional theory analyses reveal that the high activity originates from incorporated (N2)− ions at Co–Ba–Al interfacial sites, where the combination of Ba and Al plays distinct roles in N2 activation and NHx formation, respectively. These findings not only provide a strategy for stabilizing metastable crystal structures through the incorporation of diverse anionic species but also demonstrate a unique cooperative mechanism for efficient ammonia synthesis mediated by highly activated molecular (N2)− ions.

title:
Discovering Underpotentially
Deposited Crystalline
Sodium Metal Nanoparticles on the Surface of Hard Carbon Anodes
content:
Abstract
Sodium-ion batteries are attractive candidates for low-cost and scalable energy storage in which hard carbon (HC) anodes are used. However, sodium (Na) metal plating in HC anodes at voltages above the plating potential remains a critical problem. The location and spatial distribution of crystalline sodium (c-Na) metal nanoparticles, the clusters associated with Na storage in HCs, are important for understanding this underpotential plating behavior but remain unclear. Here, we implement a cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and electron tomography (cryo-ET) workflow that directly localizes c-Na metal clusters in sodiated HC samples: cryo-ET maps nanoscale three-dimensional (3D) distributions, while cryo-EM resolves local structure and chemistry. Our workflow reveals that c-Na metal clusters reside predominantly on the surfaces or near surfaces of individual HC particles. This finding challenges existing interpretations in the literature that locate the c-Na metal clusters within closed nanopores in the bulk of the HC, presumably because prior characterization using nonimaging techniques and two-dimensional (2D) projection images associated with traditional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) lacks the spatial 3D information necessary to resolve the full spatial distribution. Our discovery is an important step toward explaining the underpotential plating phenomenon of Na metal in HC anodes, suggesting that particle-level surface and near-surface interfaces are relevant targets to mitigate plating alongside bulk-pore, electrode, and electrolyte/interphase design.

title:
Continuous-Flow Irradiation
Facilitates Catalyst-Free
Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
content:
Abstract
Converting methane to methanol (MTM) holds far-reaching practical implications, yet achieving both high productivity and high selectivity remains a longstanding challenge owing to the inertness of methane and the susceptibility of methanol to overoxidation. Here, we propose a continuous-flow irradiation system (CIS) by coupling radiation technology and flow chemistry for efficient MTM under ambient conditions. High-energy radiation promises direct methane activation in an oxidant-independent and catalyst-free manner with high efficiency, which enables its integration with continuous-flow synthesis that decouples CH4 activation from methanol formation in time and space, thereby preventing overoxidation and undesirable cascade side reactions. The CIS–MTM achieves a superior methanol production rate (68.3 μmol·h–1, at a dose rate of 7.2 kGy·min–1, 83.2 RH%, CH4 flow rate 60 mL·min–1) than most existing indirect activation routes, with economic scalability comparable to industrial methods. This work introduces radiation technology as a potential direct activation method for methane conversion.

title:
Cryogenically Flexible
Organic Single-Crystal Heterostructures
via Molecular Alloying for Advanced Optical Tuning
content:
Abstract
Organic single-crystal heterostructures (OSCHs) constitute a promising platform for advanced flexible optoelectronics, yet imparting mechanical flexibility to these multiblock systems, especially given the susceptibility to failure at the interfaces between individual crystal segments, remains challenging. This obstacle is particularly aggravated at cryogenic temperatures, where the freezing of vibrational motion may cause brittleness and lead to mechanical failure. Herein, we describe an epitaxial growth strategy using molecular alloys for the fabrication of crystals of cryogenically flexible two-color (blue–cyan–blue) triblock heterostructures, prepared by growing triphenylene (TP) segments onto perylene (PER)-doped alloy seed crystals via crystallization under controlled cooling. The compatibility between the host and guest molecules provides interfaces with low defect densities. Analysis of the crystal structure reveals an abundance of weak intermolecular interactions that are thought to enable the reversible elastic deformation observed at both 298 and 77 K, thereby preventing cracking. Simultaneously, efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) between TP and PER enables continuous emission tuning and doping-ratio-controlled programmability of the optoelectronic properties. The resulting heterostructures not only support low-loss active optical waveguiding and programmable multichannel optical logic and information encoding but also remain fully operational for optical transduction during bending under cryogenic conditions. This work establishes a general molecular alloying approach to structures that integrate low-temperature mechanical compliance with sophisticated photonic functionalities, providing a pathway to deformable, multiemissive optoelectronics elements that remain operational in extreme environments.

title:
Extended Active Learning-Guided
Design of Multi-Component
Electrolytes with Opposing Cosolvent Properties for Aqueous Zinc-Ion
Batteries
content:
Abstract
Multi-component electrolytes offer expanded tunability over electrochemical properties, yet their rational design is constrained by a lack of generalizable principles. Intricate intercomponent interactions obscure the relationship between the molecular properties and battery performance, rendering material selection and compositional optimization intractable. Here, we present an extended active learning-guided framework to efficiently navigate the vast materials space and refine formulations for tri-solvent-based electrolytes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries with minimal experimental workload. Specifically, co-solvent candidates are clustered by molecular properties; co-solvents are then selected, and their pairwise combinations undergo rigorous formulation optimization. Our data-driven approach discovered a nonintuitive electrolyte composition: combining co-solvents with fundamentally opposing properties. This unique formulation, which disrupts the hydrogen-bonded network while reconstructing the solvation structure, enables Zn||NH4V4O10 full-cells to retain 90.2% capacity after 1,000 cycles. This study unveils the possibility of using active learning to discover unconventional electrolyte formulations that would otherwise be infeasible to identify through human insights.

title:
Catalytic Uncaging
of Anticancer Drugs via a Buchner
Ring Expansion
content:
Abstract
Selective drug activation in living systems remains a central challenge in targeted cancer therapy. Bioorthogonal catalysis addresses this by using abiotic transition-metal catalysts to unmask prodrugs at the tumor site, but the repertoire of suitable reactions remains limited. Here, we exploit the Buchner ring-expansion as a new uncaging strategy, in which a metal-carbene catalyzes a regioselective intramolecular ring-expansion followed by spontaneous 1,6-elimination to release a caged payload─a cascade with no biological equivalent. The iridium porphyrin complex [Ir(mPIX)Me] catalyzes this reaction at nanomolar concentrations, and the platform can accommodate structurally diverse payloads. As a proof of concept, functionalization with a bivalent human carbonic anhydrase IX (hCA IX) inhibitor enabled tumor-selective release of epirubicin (Epi) in a cancer cell model. This work thus delineates a new reaction class to the growing toolkit of transition-metal-mediated bioorthogonal chemistry.

title:
Beyond
Linker Length: Three-Dimensional Linker Geometry
Governs Flexibility in Zn–Triazolate MOFs
content:
Abstract
Flexible metal–organic frameworks undergo cooperative structural transformations that underpin applications in molecular separations, sensing, and gas storage; however, the molecular origins of framework flexibility remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the role of linker geometry in directing the structural response of a family of isoreticular Zn–triazolate pillared-layer MOFs incorporating cubane (cdc), bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane (pdc), and bicyclo[2.2.2]octane (boct) dicarboxylate linkers. Variable-temperature and in situ CO2 powder X-ray diffraction, variable-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction, gas adsorption measurements, and machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations reveal fundamentally different mechanical responses despite the frameworks possessing closely related architectures. The cdc framework exhibits reversible cooperative breathing, the pdc analogue undergoes pathway-dependent structural reorganization consistent with kinetic trapping following cooling of the activated framework to 77 K, whereas the boct framework accommodates deformation through continuous elastic distortion without discrete phase transitions. Computational analysis demonstrates that these contrasting behaviors arise primarily from the manner in which linker geometry governs strain accommodation within the flexible Zn–triazolate sheets, rather than from the deformation of the linker itself. These results establish structure–mechanics relationships across this family of flexible MOFs and demonstrate that subtle changes in molecular geometry provide a powerful strategy for programming cooperative structural behavior.

title:
A Photosensitizer Bearing
an Asymmetric “Push-Pull”
Bipyridine Ligand Enhances Excited State Electron Transfer
content:
Abstract
Herein we report RuII photosensitizers that bear a single “push-pull” ligand designed to polarize charge on a single pyridine ring of 2,2′-bipyridine (bpy) in the metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) excited state for enhanced excited state electron transfer. The photosensitizers have the general structure [Ru(dtb)2(4-CO2H,4′-R-bpy)]2+, where R is –H (RuHcb), −CF3 (RuFcb), and −CH3 (RuMcb) and dtb is 4,4′-(tert-butyl)2-bpy. These photosensitizers were synthesized, characterized spectroscopically and electrochemically, and contrasted with [Ru(dtb)2(dcb)]2+ (RuDcb) that bears the more common dicarboxylic acid ligand, Dcb = 4,4′-(CO2H)2-bipyridine. When anchored to mesoporous TiO2 thin films in a 0.1 M LiClO4/CH3CN electrolyte, RuMcb|TiO2 displayed the largest excited state electron injection yield ϕinj = 0.90 and, generally, ϕinj decreased as R became more electron withdrawing. RuDcb|TiO2 displayed a significantly lower ϕinj = 0.80. Transient absorption spectra recorded on ps and ns time scales and spectroelectrochemical data revealed that ∼70% of the total ϕinj for RuMcb occurred on a sub ps time scale that could not be kinetically resolved, only 20% occurred on this same time scale for RuDcb. Quantum chemical simulations were utilized to characterize the charge transfer excited states, the surface binding, and the interfacial electron transfer kinetics. Apart from RuFcb, the data reveal that the push–pull ligand had little impact on the ground state and a significant one on the MLCT excited state, polarizing charge on a sub-ps time scale for more efficient interfacial electron transfer. More broadly, the data reveals that push–pull ligands can be optimized for excited state electron transfer reactivity.

title:
Molecular Diversity
Generation via Selective Enzymatic
C–CN Bond Scission
content:
Abstract
Selective removal of functional groups offers a powerful route to streamline molecular design and generate structural diversity. The use of such deletion strategies has surged in organic synthesis, yet achieving these transformations with high selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we present a photoenzymatic platform for stereocontrolled C–CN bond cleavage of malononitriles, enabling access to diverse chiral nitriles. Directed evolution of the flavin-dependent enzyme OYE1 yielded a variant that efficiently converted a wide range of geminal dinitriles, affording products in high yields (up to >99%) and enantioselectivities (up to 3:97 e.r.). The platform was further extended to a one-pot cascade combining Michael addition with enzymatic decyanation. Mechanistic studies revealed a pathway involving a benzyl radical intermediate (Int1), followed by a carbanion species (Int2). This work establishes the first photobiocatalytic cyano group deletion strategy and provides a modular approach for sustainable synthesis of valuable chiral nitrile scaffolds.

title:
Electroenzymatic Cascade
Enables Amino Acid Synthesis
through Simultaneous Nitrite Reduction and NADH Regeneration
content:
Abstract
Amino acids are central to life and the chemical industry, yet their sustainable synthesis remains a challenge. An electroenzymatic cascade offers a promising alternative by combining the electron/proton transfer capability of electrocatalysis with the exceptional specificity of biocatalysis. Here we present a conceptually distinct electroenzymatic cascade platform that integrates electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction, NADH regeneration, and enzymatic reductive amination. Using l-glutamate (l-Glu) as a model, we demonstrate that with Cu nanowires as the bifunctional electrocatalyst, the system generates NH4+ and biologically active NADH in situ, driving the production of l-Glu under mild conditions. The coupled cascade not only shifts the reaction equilibrium forward but also provides a favorable orientation and a proton-rich environment for the bioactive cofactor, boosting overall selectivity of bioactive NADH. The modular design allows straightforward adaptation to diverse substrates and electrodes, demonstrating the broad generality of this platform. This work establishes a sustainable and versatile strategy for amino acid synthesis and opens new directions for electroenzymatic production of nitrogen-containing chemicals.

title:
Stable
N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Derived α-Diimine
Radical Cations with Anionic Nitrogen Character
content:
Abstract
Nitrogen-centered radicals possessing substantial anionic character have remained highly challenging to isolate because of their intrinsic electronic instability in the absence of metal coordination. Herein, we report a family of stable N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-derived α-diimine radical cations that constitute a rare class of persistent organic radicals featuring pronounced anionic nitrogen-centered radical character. Combined crystallographic, EPR, electrochemical, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal an unusual electronic structure in which the molecular framework is formally cationic whereas both the unpaired electron and substantial negative charge are predominantly localized on the α-diimine nitrogen atoms. These radicals exhibit remarkable stability, undergo selective proton- and hydrogen-atom-transfer reactions, and participate in fully reversible, stepwise interconversion among dicationic, radical cationic, and neutral redox states without degradation of the molecular framework. Two-electron reduction induces reversible C–N bond formation to generate either an azetidinimine or a zwitterionic structure, with their relative stability governed by remote electronic substituents. Variable-temperature spectroscopy, UV–Vis analysis, and DFT calculations reveal dynamic solution-state equilibria that can be thermodynamically tuned through peripheral electronic modulation. These findings establish a new design principle for persistent nitrogen-centered radicals and reveal how redox state, charge distribution, spin localization, and reversible covalent bond reorganization can be coupled within a metal-free molecular framework.

title:
Catalytic Asymmetric
Diels–Alder Reaction of
β,β-Disubstituted Enals with Cyclopentadiene: Syntheses
of (−)-Camphene, (−)-β-Santalene, and (−)-( Z )-β-Santalol
content:
Abstract
Despite the long and rich history of the Diels–Alder reaction, certain aspects of its scope still remain remarkably underexplored. Most prominently, reactions with β,β-disubstituted enals as dienophiles are scarcely represented in the literature. The first general and highly enantioselective method, enabled by a strongly acidic and confined imidodiphosphorimidate organocatalyst, is reported here. The reaction tolerates a broad range of enals, including substrates with functional groups and complex alkenyl substituents, delivering the corresponding cycloadducts in good yields and excellent enantioselectivity. The synthetic utility of the method is further highlighted by concise asymmetric total syntheses of (−)-camphene, (−)-β-santalene, and (−)-(Z)-β-santalol from inexpensive starting materials.

title:
Living
Spatially Organized Hybrid Condensates for
Efficient Light-Driven CO 2 -to-Chemical Conversion
content:
Abstract
Light-driven CO2-to-chemical conversion presents a sustainable route for biomanufacturing, yet the performance of photosynthetic biohybrid systems remains fundamentally constrained by disorganized biotic–abiotic interfaces, which result in inefficient photoelectron transfer, low carbon production, and substantial cellular toxicity. Here, we report a spatially organized intracellular biohybrid system that enables the light-powered conversion of CO2 to 2,3-butanediol inEscherichia coli. Inspired by the algal pyrenoid, we constructed a TiO2/RuBisCO hybrid condensate (TRHC) by integrating protein liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) with in situ biomimetic mineralization. This spatially defined condensate physically clusters light-harvesting and carbon-fixing modules, thereby facilitating direct photoelectron transfer and contributing to improved long-term cellular robustness under continuous illumination. The TRHC achieved an apparent quantum yield of 12.4% and reduced the light-induced cellular mortality by 64%. By providing a robust photoelectron supply for CO2 assimilation, the integrated system attains a 2,3-butanediol yield of 1.38 mol/mol from the consumed glucose. Moreover, under illuminated fed-batch fermentation, the platform maintains sustained biosynthetic activity over 5 days, producing 62.11 g/L of 2,3-butanediol. This LLPS-guided strategy offers a generalizable framework for engineering efficient biotic-abiotic interfaces in solar-driven biomanufacturing.

title:
Impact of
Polymer Ripening Degree on Fluidity Control
and Enhanced Oil Recovery in Heterogeneous Reservoirs
content:
Abstract
The performance and evaluation methods of polymers with different ripening degrees in enhanced oil recovery were investigated in this paper, which can provide guidance for reducing the viscosity loss during polymer injection in the oilfield. The results show that the indoor complete ripening time of the polymer was set as 50 min. The storage modulus and loss modulus of polymer systems with 60% and 80% ripening degrees are higher than those with a 100% ripening degree, indicating that incompletely ripened polymer systems exhibit superior viscoelasticity. For the fully ripened systems, polymer molecular chains unfold completely, while incompletely ripened systems restrict solvent penetration and retain unhydrated micellar particles, which directly affect the seepage resistance and oil flooding recoveries. Capillary shear can further promote the ripening of the polymer unripened micelles and increase the apparent viscosity of the polymer solution. Compared with the polymer with a 100% ripening degree, higher resistance coefficients and residual resistance coefficients can be established by the polymer systems with 60% and 80% ripening degrees. In heterogeneous porous media, incompletely ripened polymer systems exhibit an excellent plugging and flooding performance owing to the residual undissolved micellar particles, which enhance the fluid uptake in low-permeability layers to improve oil recoveries. As validated by quantitative particle-size and image analyses, whether it is a macrodisplacement or microdisplacement experiment, when the incompletely ripened polymer is used, the effective viscosity of the flooding fluid can be improved and the areal sweep efficiency can be increased to enhance the oil recovery. Thus, incompletely ripened polymers show promising potential for oil flooding.

title:
Molecular
Design Pathways of Phenanthroline-Based
Interwell Water Tracers for Oilfield Applications
content:
Abstract
Interwell water tracer tests are critical for characterizing reservoir connectivity and flow behavior during waterflood and enhanced oil recovery operations. Existing tracers, however, are often limited by analytical complexity and challenges in scaling to multiwell deployments. This work presents a molecular design strategy for phenanthroline-based, lanthanide-sensitized interwell tracers by systematically examining how backbone functionalization governs photophysical performance, chemical robustness, analytical detectability, and reservoir-relevant transport behavior. A focused library of phenanthroline derivatives was synthesized and evaluated to decouple the roles of chelating and solubilizing functionalities. Photophysical characterization shows that while the phenanthroline antenna is broadly preserved across the derivative set, efficient Eu3+ sensitization and extended excited-state lifetimes require incorporation of a 2,9-dicarboxylate coordination motif. Sulfonation alone does not enable effective ligand-to-metal energy transfer. In contrast, combining sulfonation with dicarboxylate chelation in 5-((3-sulfopropyl)amino)-1,10-phenanthroline-2,9-dicarboxylic acid (SA-PDCA) produces strong Eu3+ emission, favorable excited-state stabilization, and improved aqueous compatibility. SA-PDCA is detected optically at ppb-level concentrations and is efficiently recovered from produced-water matrices via solid-phase extraction with substantial retention of signal intensity. Hydrothermal stability testing demonstrates that substituent identity and attachment mode strongly influence chemical robustness under high-temperature, high-salinity conditions. Coreflood experiments conducted under coinjection conditions showed that SA-PDCA exhibited transport behavior comparable to dipicolinic acid, with near-quantitative apparent recovery in carbonate rock. Collectively, these results establish SA-PDCA as a promising lead tracer candidate and define generalizable design principles for advanced reservoir surveillance applications.

title:
Postcombustion
CO 2  Capture in Offshore
FPSO Systems: Lifetime Simulation and Assessment of Perspectives and
Challenges
content:
Abstract
The present study evaluated the technical impact of incorporating an amine-based postcombustion CO2 capture unit (CCS) into FPSO (floating production, storage, and offloading) units throughout their entire operational lifetime, considering different processing capacities (100 and 250 kbpd of liquids), different gas-oil ratios (150 and 300 Sm3/Sm3), and different reservoir fluid CO2 contents (3 and 60%, molar basis). A total of 192 process simulations were performed, including simple cycle (SC), simple cycle with CCS (SC + CCS), and combined cycle with CCS (CC + CCS) configurations. The results demonstrated challenges associated with CCS unit underutilization: an average underutilization of 27% was observed, exceeding 60% during the final years of operation in all of the simulated cases. Zero underutilization was achieved in all cases only when the nominal CCS capacity was defined as 30% of the maximum exhaust gas flow rate produced in each case. For cases in which the CCS unit was designed with a full-flue-gas capture ambition for the FPSO, i.e., capable of processing up to 100% of the maximum exhaust gas flow rate generated in each case, the required CCS capacities reached up to 12.5 and 22 MMSm3/day in the SC + CCS configuration for fluids containing 3 and 60% CO2, respectively, and up to 12.1 and 18.2 MMSm3/day in the CC + CCS configuration. Replacing the SC configuration with the CC configuration in the presence of CCS resulted in reductions in cumulative emissions (over the entire operational lifetime) of up to 8.2 and 96 kt for the cases with 3 and 60% CO2, respectively. Considering the limitations associated with heat recovery availability (without the inclusion of an additional furnace) for the implementation of CCS and/or combined-cycle systems, it was observed that for the field containing 60% CO2, cumulative CO2 recovery over the installation lifetime ranged from 79 to 90% under the full-flue-gas capture design scenario. Integration of an auxiliary furnace provided limited benefits for the SC + CCS configuration. For the field containing 3% CO2, the cumulative CO2 recovery ranged from 38 to 80% across the simulated cases.

title:
Dimensionless
Scaling of First-Cycle Huff-n-Puff Hydrocarbon
Recovery and CO 2  Storage in Shale Reservoirs
content:
Abstract
Cyclic CO2 injection is the key component of carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) that enhances hydrocarbon recovery while sequestering CO2, contributing to global greenhouse gas mitigation. However, its optimization remains challenging because the process is governed by numerous interacting variables with nonlinear and competing effects, limiting the transferability of optimized parameters across reservoir systems. To address this, for the first time, this study applies dimensional analysis to identify the key dimensionless groups and establish physically interpretable scaling relations governing CO2 injection performance, enabling optimization with substantially reduced computational cost. A species-based mass transport model incorporating inhomogeneous fluid distribution induced by fluid–solid interactions is used to simulate cyclic CO2 injection and generate a comprehensive data set for dimensional analysis. Based on the Vaschy–Buckingham Pi theorem, dimensional analysis reveals key dimensionless groups governing hydrocarbon recovery (RF) and CO2 storage (EF), including response-specific Fourier numbers (FoR, FoS), diffusivity ratios (RDR, RDS), fluid–solid friction modulus (φR, φS), together with time ratio (RT), normalized drawdown pressure (PD), and relative fluid–solid interaction coefficient (χ). The RF scaling relation identifies a critical point, i.e., ψRC = 0.0015, separating mixing-dominated and mixing-limited regimes, providing a calibrated transition criterion for identifying diminishing recovery gains. The critical point ψSC = 0.0025 in the EF scaling relation marks the transition between retention-growth and retention-limited regimes, beyond which additional gains in postcycle CO2 retention diminish. This study provides practical guidance for cyclic CO2 injection in ultratight reservoirs, supporting more effective CO2 utilization for hydrocarbon recovery and improved CO2 storage performance.

title:
Thickeners
for Anhydrous CO 2  Fracturing
Fluids: From Molecular Design to Field Applications
content:
Abstract
Conventional hydraulic fracturing consumes massive amounts of water and causes severe formation damage. Anhydrous CO2 fracturing fluids offer a promising low-carbon alternative. Nevertheless, the low intrinsic viscosity of CO2 severely restricts proppant transport and complex fracture propagation, hindering large-scale field application. Over the past three decades, research on CO2 thickeners has evolved from empirical screening to mechanism-guided molecular design, with the thickening paradigm shifting from simple polymer chain entanglement to dynamic supramolecular self-assembly networks. However, systematic and critical reviews focusing on their development, key challenges, and paradigm limitations are rare. This paper presents a comprehensive review of CO2 thickeners, covering their molecular design, synthesis approaches, performance control, thickening mechanisms, and field applications. We summarize their evolution from fluorinated and siloxane-based polymers to hydrocarbon modifiers, supramolecular small molecules, and surfactant systems, and clarify the intrinsic thickening mechanisms of each category. Field case studies show that although siloxane-based and fluorinated systems exhibit application potential, they are still constrained by strong cosolvent dependence or environmental persistence risks. To address these bottlenecks, this review proposes prospective development directions, including smart-responsive materials, bioinspired green chemistries, and AI-assisted inverse molecular design. This review is expected to provide a theoretical reference and practical guidance for the development of high-efficiency, eco-friendly, and field-scalable CO2 fracturing technologies.

title: Microphase-Engineered Homologous Ion-Exchange Layers for High-Current-Density Bipolar Membrane Electrolysis
content:
Abstract
Bipolar membranes (BPMs) maintain separated acidic and alkaline environments via water dissociation at the junction, but high-current-density operation remains challenging because rapid hydrated H+/OH– migration away from the junction must be coupled with sufficient water replenishment toward it. A transport imbalance between these opposing processes causes interfacial dehydration and limits long-term operation. Here, we develop microphase-engineered homologous ion-exchange layers to balance this coupled transport. These layers are fabricated from homologous multiblock poly(biphenyl alkylene) ionomers sharing a common backbone and block architecture, promoting interlayer compatibility and interconnected ionic domains. The hydrated pathways accelerate water replenishment and ion transport, thereby maintaining a stably hydrated junction. The resulting BPM enables pure-water electrolysis at 2.11 V at 1000 mA cm–2 and sustains high-purity hydrogen production for over 1100 h at 500 mA cm–2. This work establishes molecularly engineered ion-exchange layers as an effective approach for improving mass transport in high-current-density BPM systems.

title: Decoupled Water Electrolysis with an Air-Stable Zwitterionic Azo Mediator
content:
Abstract
Decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) separates H2 and O2 evolution, improving safety and flexibility under intermittent renewable electricity, but requires durable, oxygen-tolerant redox mediators. Here we evaluate 4,4′-azo-bis(1-pyridinium-3-propane-sulfonate) (ABPS), a zwitterionic azo molecule, as an electron-coupled proton buffer for acidic DWE. Its azo/hydrazo core supports reversible two-electron/two-proton chemistry at 0.81 V vs RHE, while zwitterionic substituents provide high aqueous solubility and suppress crossover through low-cost sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membranes. Reduced H2ABPS shows no detectable oxidation after 90 days in air or during >5 h of continuous pure-O2 bubbling. Symmetric flow-cell cycling over 1000 h yields a capacity-fade rate below 1% year–1. With commercial catalysts at room temperature, decoupled flow cells reach 1.2 A cm–2 and operate for >200 h at 500 mA cm–2 with near-quantitative Faradaic efficiencies while producing high-purity H2 and O2. These results establish zwitterionic azo chemistry as an oxygen-tolerant, durable platform for high-rate decoupled hydrogen production.

title: Operando X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Reveals Oxide Solid Electrolyte Stability against Electrochemically Plated Lithium
content:
Abstract
X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has revealed many possible Li-induced interfacial reactions in solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but most in situ studies form Li|electrolyte interfaces through non-electrochemical Li deposition, including evaporation, sputtering, or electron-beam-induced deposition. These routes may introduce additional energy that activates reaction pathways not accessed during electrochemical Li plating. Here, we use lab-based operando XPS to directly evaluate oxide solid-state electrolyte stability during electrochemical Li formation. Using this approach, we find sharply different responses for two representative oxide SSEs: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2–x(PO4)3 (LATP) is reduced upon Li plating, forming a Li+/Ti3+-rich mixed-conducting interphase that partially relaxes through coupled ionic–electronic redistribution, whereas garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) shows no spectroscopically resolvable Zr or La reduction. This work represents the first direct operando XPS evaluation of SSE stability against electrochemically plated Li metal.

title: Engineered Fe 2 O 3 /TiO 2 /Carbon-Dots Heterostructures for Enhanced Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
content:
Abstract
Hematite (α-Fe2O3) is an abundant, low-cost visible-light absorber and a leading photoanode candidate for solar-driven water splitting, yet its conversion efficiency remains constrained by poor charge transport, fast electron–hole recombination, and sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics. Here, we engineer a Fe2O3/TiO2/Carbon-dot (C-dot) photoanode built on an FTO substrate that addresses these bottlenecks through a defined layer architecture: hydrothermally grown Fe2O3 nanorods provide visible-light absorption, a sol–gel-deposited mesoporous TiO2 overlayer passivates the hematite surface, and finally solvothermally grown C-dots decorate the outer surface to drive interfacial charge transfer. Structural and chemical characterization confirms a well-integrated, intimately contacted heterostructure, while optical measurements show that C-dot incorporation broadens visible-light harvesting without altering the underlying optical band gap (∼2.1 eV) indicating that any performance gain originates from charge-transport rather than band-structure effects. Under photoelectrochemical testing, the Fe2O3/TiO2/C-dots photoanode delivers substantially higher OER photocurrent than the Fe2O3/TiO2 baseline across the full UV-to-visible illumination range, with simulated-solar photocurrent density increasing by approximately 2.5-fold at neutral pH and by approximately 3.4-fold under alkaline conditions, pH 14, where OER kinetics are most favorable. The device sustains stable, reproducible photocurrent over multi-hour continuous solar illumination in both electrolytes, supporting its operational robustness under realistic water-splitting conditions. Mechanistically, Mott–Schottky analysis shows that C-dot incorporation more than doubles the carrier density (from 1.6 × 1020 to 3.3 × 1020 cm–3), while electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals a ∼27% reduction in interfacial charge-transfer resistance, together identifying enhanced carrier density and accelerated interfacial charge transfer, rather than band-edge modification, as the origin of the improved device performance. These results establish C-dot functionalization as a simple, scalable strategy for boosting the photocurrent and operational stability of Fe2O3/TiO2 photoanodes, with direct relevance to the design of higher-performing, low-cost solar-to-fuel conversion devices for water oxidation and solar hydrogen production.

title: Composite Solid Polymer Electrolytes Based on PEO and Surface-Modified Al 2 O 3  Fillers for Solid-State Sodium Ion Batteries
content:
Abstract
Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based solid polymer electrolytes suffer from low ionic conductivity and limited Na+ transport capability, which restrict their application in solid-state sodium metal batteries. Herein, a Na+-coordinating filler (Al2O3@KHMF) is prepared by grafting organic chains onto the Al2O3 surface through silane coupling followed by a Schiff-base reaction. The grafted chains, bearing imine nitrogen and carbonyl oxygen groups, provide abundant coordination sites for Na+ ions and simultaneously enhance the interfacial suitability for the polymer matrix. These functional groups facilitate NaTFSI dissociation and weaken the interaction between Na+ ions and PEO chains, thereby promoting Na+ transport. Consequently, the optimized PEO-NaTFSI-Al2O3@KHMF composite electrolyte achieves an ionic conductivity of 5.10 × 10–3 S cm–1 and a Na+ transference number of 0.44 at 60 °C. The electrolyte enables stable Na plating/stripping for over 800 h at 0.1 mA cm–2. Furthermore, the assembled Na3V2(PO4)3||Na cell delivers a reversible capacity of 74.7 mAh g–1 after 200 cycles at 2 C, demonstrating enhanced cycling stability when operating at a high rate. This work offers an effective molecular interface engineering strategy for developing high-performance solid-state sodium metal batteries.

title: Synergistic Trait of Dual Hole Transport Materials in High-Performance Inverted Tin Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
Abstract
PEDOT:PSS is widely employed as a hole transport layer (HTL) in inverted tin-based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs) owing to its high optical transmittance and excellent compatibility with tin perovskites (TPsks). However, its relatively low hole mobility and suboptimal energy-level alignment with TPsk limit device performance. In contrast, the inorganic semiconductor CuO exhibits superior hole mobility, low electron affinity, high transparency, and adjustable energy levels, but suffers from poor film morphology and inadequate interfacial compatibility with TPsks. A CuO/PEDOT:PSS dual-layer HTL (CuPE) was developed to synergistically combine the advantages of inorganic CuO and polymeric PEDOT:PSS while mitigating their respective drawbacks. TPSCs incorporating the CuPE-400 (when CuO was annealed at 400 °C) HTL achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 12.24%, which is significantly higher than those (8.72 and 8.65%, respectively) of devices employing either CuO-400 or PEDOT:PSS alone. CuPE-400-based devices retained 82% of their initial PCE after 1,584 h of storage in a glovebox, outperforming CuO-400 and PEDOT devices, which retained only 63 and 69% of their initial efficiencies, respectively. The excellent photovoltaic performance of CuPE-400 is attributed to its high hole mobility and low trap density, achieved through the partial interpenetration of CuO grains and PEDOT:PSS polymer chains (as revealed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) depth profile analysis) to form a dense CuPE-400 film as well as a good-quality TPsk film, which was coated on CuPE-400. Notably, when CuO-250 was annealed at 250 °C, the CuPE-250-based cell still exhibited a PCE of 12.00%, which is very close to that of the device based on CuPE-400. These results demonstrate the potential of CuO-based HTLs for low-temperature processing.

title: Enhancing CO 2  Capture and H 2  Enrichment by Coupling THF with Kinetic Promoters for Hydrate-Based CO 2 /H 2  Separation: Experimental Investigation & Chemical Potential Driven Kinetic Model
content:
Abstract
Hydrate-based CO2/H2 separation provides an attractive route for pre-combustion CO2 capture with simultaneous H2 enrichment; however, its practical application remains constrained by sluggish hydrate formation and the limited understanding of environmentally benign kinetic promoters under CO2-rich fuel-gas conditions. In this study, we first examine the effect of the thermodynamic promoter tetrahydrofuran (THF) on hydrate formation from a CO2/H2 (60:40) mixture at 3.0 MPa and establish 5.56 mol % as the optimum concentration under the investigated experimental conditions. Increasing the THF concentration from 3.0 to 5.56 mol % increases gas uptake from 15.98 to 20.93 mmol/mol H2O and reduces T90 from 74.5 to 18.5 min over 280.2–283.2 K. The optimized THF system is subsequently coupled with three hydrophobic amino acids (0.5 wt % l-Methionine, l-Leucine, and l-Tryptophan) to promote hydrate growth. Their effects are evaluated experimentally and further interpreted using a chemical-potential-driven kinetic model for structure II (sII) hydrate formation. The amino acids influence hydrate growth in a molecule-dependent manner, with l-Leucine and l-Methionine exhibiting the most favourable kinetic and hydrate-yield characteristics. Despite the enhanced formation behaviour, the preferential separation of CO2 is retained: gas chromatographic analysis shows 92.7–94.7% CO2 in the hydrate phase, while the residual vapour is enriched to as much as 59.3% H2. By combining THF and amino-acid-assisted promotion, and chemical-potential-based kinetic modelling, this study links molecular-level promotion with macroscopic hydrate growth and phase selectivity in a CO2-rich CO2/H2 system. The findings provide a basis for developing hydrate-based separation processes that couple CO2 capture with H2 enrichment.

title: Demonstrating the Generality of Kerr-Gated Raman Spectroscopy Measurements of High Charge States in Graphitic Electrodes for Li-Ion Batteries
content:
Abstract
Herein, the systematic application of the Kerr-gated Raman spectroscopy technique to track lithium intercalation into Li-ion graphite electrodes is reported under different operando, in situ, and ex situ experimental conditions with different graphitic electrode materials and electrolyte material formulations, through multiple cycles. The results revealed a broad generality of (i) the capability of the technique to resolve the characteristic G-band of graphite electrodes even at high charge states (high states of lithiation) and (ii) the sensitivity of the shift in the observed G-band to the state of electrochemical lithiation at high charge states during the transition from stage 2 to stage 1 (0.5 ≤ x ≤1 for LixC6). The shifted G-band was observed in highly lithiated electrodes comprising different graphite sources and conventional Li-ion-type electrolyte formulations and was further replicated using a noncommercial ionic liquid-based electrolyte formulation. Additionally, the persistence of the G-band (and the related shift as a function of charge) was replicated in many ex situ samples across 10 cycles, further evidencing the potential of this technique as a diagnostic tool to track high states of charge in cycled graphite-based negative electrodes for Li-ion batteries.
